Right next to Gangseo-gu Office Station, there is Daejeo Eco Park, a representative, natural, ecological, water-friendly space in Busan. 

The vast space offers an unrealistic, beautiful view of mustard flowers in the spring, as well as sunflowers and cosmos in the summer. In the fall, romantic pink muhly grasses decorate the area, making the park a must-see destination in Busan.

The view of Daejeo Eco Park in harmony with the Nakdonggang River is stimulating and impressive.

item.TITLE: Maekdo Ecological Park
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit No.1 of Daejeo Station on Busan Metro Line No. 3 → Get on Busan-Gimhae Light Rail Transit (Towards Sasang)
→ Exit No. 1 of Seobusan Utongjigu Station → Transfer to town bus Gangseogu 13 at Seobusan Utongjigu Station Bus Stop
→ A 6-minute walk from Maekdo Ecological Park Bus Stop
Parking: Maekdo Ecological Park Public Parking Lot
item.MIDDLE_SIZE_RM1: Disabled restrooms; disabled parking; wheelchair accessible
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
There are six distinctive ecological parks on the riverside of the Nakdonggang River in the west of Busan. The Maekdo Ecological Park is not well-known among these ecological parks, but it’s a well-loved park for its natural beauty. Walking is the best way to look around Maekdo Ecological Park. Since the park is not that big, walking through it slowly will take no more than 1 hour and 30 minutes. 

Three routes are recommended to the first-time visitors to the Maekdo Ecological Park.
The first route to take is the Cherry Blossom Road built on the causeway and the Metasequoia Road below. Along the causeway, large cherry and metasequoia trees grow beautifully, and while cherry blossoms are in full bloom in spring, late summer and autumn is a wonderful time for leisurely strolls.

The second route to take is Waterside Trail along the Nakdonggang River. The riverside has walking trails and rest areas about 10 minutes away from the park. Several paths lead right next to the Nakdonggang River, so you can walk while listening to the reeds sway in the wind.

The last route to take is a deck road built between the lotus garden and the aquatic botanical garden in the middle of the ecological park. A walk on the deck is a great way to check out the lotus flowers and various aquatic plants.

item.TITLE: Golden Sunset Bridge
item.TRFC_INFO:
A 6-minute walk from Exit 3 of Deokcheon station on Busan Metro line 2
Parking Daericheon Public Parking Lot
item.MIDDLE_SIZE_RM1: Disabled restrooms; disabled parking; wheelchair accessible
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The Golden Sunset Bridge, located at the entrance of Gupo Market, is a pedestrian bridge that connects Gupo and Hwamyeong Eco Park. As the name suggests, it is located in an excellent location to watch the sunset across the Nakdonggang River toward Gimhae.

The Golden Sunset Bridge is about four stories high, and you can climb up it by stairs. When you stand on the bridge, you can see the view of Gupo Market to Hwamyeong-dong from both sides. Also, passing on the railroad, you can see trains passing by if the time is right.

If you walk along the pedestrian bridge, there is an observatory at the end, so you can take a break and enjoy a cool breeze and a great view. At night, you can see the wonderful night view with the lighting, so if you have time, be sure to watch both the sunset and the night view.

The Golden Sunset Bridge is not that long, so it is great place to go for a light walk. If you are looking for a different tourist destination in Busan, it would be pleasant to visit here.

item.TITLE: Gamjeon Wildflower Garden
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 2, Gamjeon Station, Metro Line 2 → Transfer to Bus 138-1 at North Busan Tax Office / Gamjeon Station 
→ disembark at Gamjeon-dong Floodgate, 10 minutes by walking
Parking P11 Parking Lot at Samnak Eco Park
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Located near the Samnak Eco Park, Gamjeon Wildflower Garden is situated on the side of the Nakdonggang River where Dadaehang Road meets the Nakdongdaegyo Bridge. As the largest colony of wildflowers and aquatic plants in Busan, it is one of the best places to meet the wildflowers of Busan in summer.

Here, one can meet the green fields and summer flowers just by taking a leisurely walk along the trail. Walking in the Gamjeon Wildflower Garden is a quiet and peaceful affair, punctuated by beautiful colors of wildflowers.

Once you've had your fill of the wildflower garden, take the riverside road and stroll along the Nakdonggang River with the breeze. The unassuming river presents an intimate view of nature that, while not flashy nor extravagant, soothes one's heart.

item.TITLE: The International Coffee Museum
item.ADDR1: 380, Jungang-daero, Dong-gu, Busan (Jwacheon-dong, former Busanjin Station
item.TRFC_INFO:
2 minutes walk from Exit 8 of Busanjin station on Busan Metro Line 1
Parking: Busanjin Station public parking lot
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
On the first floor of the building, there is a special space called ‘The International Coffee Museum.’ About 2000 coffee machines from all over the world are on display, so you can see the history of coffee machines around the world in one place.

This is a space where a variety of coffee equipment, carefully collected by a coffee lover, is displayed with detailed explanations. It is an exhibition that helps give a broader understanding of the history and culture of coffee. If you apply for a 'Docent Experience' where you can listen to unique episodes together, and you can enjoy the exhibition even more. There is also a one-day class where you can experience coffee extraction and even drink it. It will be a special experience that is not easily accessible as you can watch the brewing using various coffee equipment such as siphon, percolator, biggin, Turkish, and moka pot.

Busan is well-known as a place where you can experience coffee healing with excellent natural scenery. A place where specialties and small brands coexist as well as the International Coffee Museum. Immerse yourself in the charm of Busan, the coffee city where the Global Coffee Festival is held.

item.TITLE: Park Tae-joon Museum
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 1 of Jwacheon Station on Donghae Line → Transfer to Bus 37 at Donghaeseon Jwacheon Station bus stop
→ Get off at Imnang Samgeori bus stop and walk for 2 minutes

Parking: Park Tae joon Museum Parking Lot
item.HLDY_INFO:
Mondays, January 1, the day of Seollal/Chuseok
(The following day if Monday is a holiday)
item.MIDDLE_SIZE_RM1: Disabled restrooms; disabled parking; wheelchair accessible
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The Park Tae-joon Museum, which officially opened on December 14, 2021, tells the story of POSCO, which laid the foundation for Korea's growth.

Built next to the birthplace of the late Honorary Chairman Park Tae-joon, the museum commemorates the achievements of Cheongam, who left a significant mark on the modern and contemporary history of the Republic of Korea, and investigates and studies his philosophy and thoughts. The approximately 1,200 artifacts displayed and stored in the memorial hall are valuable materials that lay out history and culture from the Japanese colonial period to the present.

What particularly attracts attention here is the memorial quote written by the late Lee O-young. 

"The reason we can now sleep on high pillows is because your blood and sweat poured into the iron factory, and the reason we can hold a child in our arms and make each person dream of tomorrow is because of you, who expanded the garden of knowledge by establishing a school.“

The Park Tae-joon Museum is renowned as a building that blends in to its surrounding landscape, using its surrounding nature as a reference point. So why don’t you take a breather, hold your child’s hand, and take a look around the exhibition hall? Spend some time reading a book at the small library of Imnang Cultural Park located inside the building. It will do you good.

item.TITLE: Dadaepo Beach Park
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 4 of Dadaepo Beach Station on Line 1 a 4-minute walk
item.MIDDLE_SIZE_RM1: Disabled restrooms; disabled parking; wheelchair accessible
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Dadaepo Beach Park, located in front of Dadaepo Beach and Morundae Peninsula, is perfect for viewing the red sunset and is considered a famous sunset spot. Dadaepo Beach Park, which extends from the Molundae public parking lot to Noeuljeong, consists of a sea stream, a grassy plaza, and a walking path filled with pine groves.

Swings and benches are installed throughout the walking trails so you can stroll around comfortably, and the seascape from here is also spectacular. Tents and mats are allowed in the pine forest, which was built in the direction of the white sand beach, and it is becoming well-known as a budget resort.

In an era where the country has over 10 million dogs, Dadaepo Beach Park has dog urinals called ‘Pettoilet’ throughout the park in line with the trend of the times!

At the end of Dadaepo Beach Park, a wide field of reeds spreads out, and the Gowooni Ecological Path is on a wooden deck above it. The night lights along the trail create a dreamy atmosphere, so it gets a thumbs up as a unique night walking course!

item.TITLE: UN Peace Park
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5 of Kyungsung Univ. ∙ Pukyong National Univ. Station on Busan Metro Line 2 → Transfer to Bus 10, 20, 22, 24, 27, 39, 131, or 155 at Kyungsung Univ. Entrance Bus Stop → Get off at Daeyeon Xi Apt. Bus Stop and walk for 1 minute
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
UN Peace Park is a neighborhood park near the UN Memorial Cemetery in Korea. It was developed after the APEC Summit 2005, gaining popularity with Busan citizens as a beautiful walking course.

It is a perfect place where you can enjoy the fresh air and beautiful scenery while taking a walk along with various facilities such as an ecological pond, lawn, trails, and ground fountain, as well as over 30,000 trees, such as pine trees and camellias, and over 30,000 eye-catching plants. It is a relaxing space and suitable for outings with family and friends.
Pettoilets, urinals only for pets, are located throughout the UN Peace Park in line with the trend of pets becoming indispensable family members. Devices that allow owners to leash their pets when using bathrooms are another attractive feature of the park.

How about taking a walk with your loved ones and friends at the UN Peace Park, which has different charms every season?

item.TITLE: Busan Central Park, a Place of Good Luck
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 6, Dong-eui University Station, Busan Metro Line 2 -> 
Transfer to Bus No. 169 at Gaegeum Jugong Apartment Bus Stop -> 
Get off at Busan Jeongjungang Park & Baegyangsan Lotte Castle Bus Stop, a 1-min walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Among the people of Busan, this park is considered to be one of the most propitious spots in the city that exudes good energy. Situated right in the middle of the city at the coordinates 35°10'4"N and 129°2'17"E, this place is believed to bring health, happiness, and wealth. and even fertility. Locals also believe that the energy of this place also affects their children to be good sons and daughters. No wonder so many locals come here to make a wish or two.

Why the coordinates? In 2001, an elementary school student was curious to know the geographic center of the city and sent the question to a SBS TV variety show called Hogisim Cheonguk (‘curiosity heaven’ in Korean) so they would find out where the exact center of the city is. 

In turn, the producers of the TV show had the Urban Affairs Research Institute of Pusan National University to pinpoint the location, which turned out to be 548-12 Buam-dong, Busanjin-gu. Afterwards, a central marker stone was erected there, and the Office of Busanjin-gu created a small park around the stone. The original park was demolished in 2018 for a housing redevelopment project, and the new one was recreated in the current location.
Its symbolic character BuJung-i also has an interesting story. BuJung-i, a compound word made by combining Busan and ‘jungang’ (‘center’ in Korean), literally represents the geographic center of Busan. 

It is a yellow chicken in the shape of a golden hen sitting on eggs. It is said that the energy of Geumjeongsan Mountain and that of Baegyangsan Mountain’s Azure Dragon of the East extended to the marker stone and woke up the sleeping chicken BuJung-i. It has the mysterious power to share its lucky energy and happiness with people living in every corner of Busan and reward those with a golden egg for making an earnest wish – only when it’s touched by the wish, of course.

The new marker stone (4.1 m wide, 3.3 m high) stands tall in the park. We hope you to stop by at this small park and take in all the good energy the place has to offer so that everything goes well for you.

item.TITLE: Bokcheonsa Temple
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 6 of Nampo Station on Busan Metro Line 1 → Transfer to bus 82 or 85 at Yeongdodaegyo-Nampo Station Bus Stop
→ Get off at Shinseon Middle School Bus Stop and walk for 16 min
Parking: Sinseon 3-dong Public Parking Lot
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Bokcheonsa Temple, located at the foot of Bongnaesan Mountain, is famous for its sunset and night view. The temple is not well-known, perhaps because of the high slope to reach to the temple, but if you visit in person, you will soon find it a stunning place. Although the temple size is not large, everywhere makes a good photo spot because of the temple’s distinctive serene atmosphere and beautiful scenery.

The main place to appreciate Bokcheonsa Temple’s night view is the Observation Deck in front of Sansingak Hall, which can be reached by the stairs beside the Daeungjeon Hall. You will see the beautiful harmonious landscape of Bokcheonsa Temple and Namhangdaegyo Bridge at the Observation Deck. It is strongly recommended to visit in time for sunset.

It is not clearly visible during the day, but at night, the candle becomes a feature and seems to fill up the dark scenery with warmth. If you stand on the railing next to Cheonwangmun Gate, you will be able to see the beautiful night view of Namhangdaegyo Bridge and Songdo, so don’t forget to stop by before you go down!

item.TITLE: Artificial Migratory Bird Habitat Myeongpum Dulle Trails
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 3 of Hadan Station on Busan Metro Line 1 → Transfer to Village Bus Gangseo-gu 17 at Hadan Station Bus Stop
→ Get off at Sinho Village Bus Stop → Walk for 5 minutes
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
I think many people still don't know about this place. 

Originally, it was a place where the general public was prohibited from entering because it was a military operation area, so it is preserved as an internal wetland, its natural state. It has been open as a trail since July 2022.

Myeongpum Dulle Trails are neither too long nor too short, so they are perfect for a leisurely walk. The Dulle Trails start right next to the sea, so you can enjoy a walk while feeling the natural sea air. Thanks to the flooring laid on the ground, it is soft and comfortable, so you can walk without feeling tired on your feet. Also, a wetland is right next to it, so you can feel a little further away from the city center. 

Unfortunately, however, it is not yet possible to enter the wetland.
The Myeongpum Dulle Trails are also connected to Galmaet Trails, and there is a small forest trail beside the road, so enjoy a walk there with your pet.

item.MAIN_TITLE: 목련꽃 가득 안은 성암사, 나만 알고 싶은 봄꽃 성지(한,영,중간,중번,일)
item.TITLE: Seongamsa Temple: A hidden gem filled with magnolias, a sanctuary of spring flowers that I wish to keep to myself
item.TRFC_INFO: Use the Exit 2 of Munhyeon Station on Busan Metro Line 2 → Transfer to Bus 138 or 101 at Munhyeon-3dong Community Service Center Station → Get off at Munhyeon Hyundai Apartment → Walk for 8 min
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Located at the foot of Galmibong Peak in Hwangnyeongsan Mountain, the quaint Seongamsa Temple stands out with its grand magnolia trees.By mid-March, as the white magnolia blossoms envelop the temple, visitors dressed in lighter and brighter attire begin to line up for their peaceful outings. Under the shade of the trees, as you gaze at the fully bloomed magnolias, it almost feels like you can hear the clear, innocent laughter of children.

'When magnolias bloom, come listen to their sound; when they fall, come to see a baby’s steps.‘ The poet Kim Ju-dae once likened the fallen petals of magnolias to a baby's feet in his poem.
When fallen petals resemble a baby's feet, making one tread carefully to avoid stepping on them, both people and landscapes transform into poetry.


The grounds of Seongamsa Temple are said to resemble a turtle laying eggs, with legends suggesting that praying at the Samseongjeon and Yongwangdang Shrines bestows offspring. Just as the plum blossoms begin to fade, the magnolias start to bloom. The scene, dotted with falling magnolia petals, carries a somewhat melancholy beauty. It is recommended to visit before the flowers fade to capture this unique moment.

item.TITLE: Ttangmoesan Red Clay Trail
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The Ttangmoesan Red Clay Trail is a hiking trail in the Hoedong Reservoir area, surrounded by a lush forest and offering panoramic views of the lake. True to its name, Ttangmoesan Red Clay Barefoot Trail allows you to feel the earth beneath your bare feet and truly connect with nature.

One moment, you're admiring the cute and colorful murals along the way, and the next, you're stepping onto the Red Clay Trail. Kick off your shoes and immerse yourself in the soft yet cool texture of the red clay. The cypress forest section of the trail is perfect for breathing in the fresh forest air.

In addition to the red clay, there are many other healing spots along the trail. One of them is the beautiful lake visible from the Palgakjeong Pavilion shelter. Pause for a moment to enjoy the scenery from the shelter. The combination of forest, lake, and dirt paths allows you to experience nature with all five senses, nourishing your body and mind.

item.TITLE: Discover Vibrant India in Korea
item.SUBTITLE: Indian Cultural Centre Busan
item.ADDR1: The India Centre, 171-1, UN-ro, Nam-gu, Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: Use the exit 1 of Daeyeon Station on the Busan Metro Line 2 → Walk for 13 minutes
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
From tea and yoga to royal cuisine, you enjoy India in the most luxurious way at the Indian Cultural Centre in Busan! The first floor of the building houses the Aap Ki Pasand SAN-CHA Tea Boutique, which offers premium Indian tea brands. Renowned worldwide, Indian tea can be savored right here in Busan with Aap Ki Pasand, considered the finest among India’s famous tea brands. This is thrilling news for tea lovers! Upon entering the boutique, you’ll be captivated by the unique charm of India, set in a clean and spacious environment. The glamorous tea packaging designs and a charming miniature of the Taj Mahal enhance the exotic aroma and ambiance.

Aap Ki Pasand SAN-CHA Tea Boutique

  • Operating Hours : Monday–Friday 10:00–19:00, Saturdays and Sundays 11:00–18:00
  • Details : About 100 types of tea available for sale (Tea Pot + Indian Dessert: KRW 10,000 / Summer Season Limited India Peach Black Tea: KRW 10,000)
  • Contact : +82-51-322-3353
The second and third floors of the building are dedicated to a yoga studio and a royal cuisine experience center, respectively. At the yoga studio, immerse yourself in Indian-style meditation, then indulge in royal Indian cuisine prepared by a chef from the Presidential Palace. You will instantly appreciate the essence of Indian luxury. However, be warned: the indulgence might just undo your yoga training as you find yourself succumbing to worldly desires!

Indian National Yoga Centre IYC

  • Operating Hours : 09:00~22:00
  • Details : The first Indian National Yoga Centre in Korea where you can receive training directly from Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga
  • Contact : +82-51-508-4254

Bhavan Indo Restaurant, Indian royal cuisine.

  • Operating Hours : 11:00~21:00
  • Details : Authentic Indian royal cuisine presented by chefs who formerly served high-ranking officials and the president. Opened to commemorate the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Korea and India.
  • Contact : +82-51-623-4259
The Indian Cultural Centre Busan is located near the UN Memorial Cemetery, the final resting place for soldiers from the Korean war. India played a significant role in the war, primarily providing medical support and caring for prisoners of war and civilians. Additionally, the Centre offers lectures on Indian culture. Learning about and experiencing Indian traditions, while reflecting on India’s supportive role during the Korean War, can be a truly enriching experience.

Indian Cultural Centre

  • Operating Hours : 9:00~19:00
  • Contact : +82-51-508-4254

item.TITLE: Want to know more about ASEAN?
item.SUBTITLE: KF ASEAN Culture House
item.TRFC_INFO:
Use Exit 2 of Jangsan Station on the Busan Metro Line 2 -> Walk for 14 minutes (Park on BF1 and pick up a parking ticket at the information desk.)
Free parking (Receive a parking ticket at the information desk)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Is ‘ASEAN’ unfamiliar but intriguing to you?
Discover more at the KF ASEAN Culture House in Busan! 

ASEAN, also known as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, is a group of ten countries in Southeast Asia (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam).
The KF ASEAN Culture House was opened to promote cultural exchange between ASEAN and Korea. It organizes various cultural events and educational and experiential programs to bring citizens closer to ASEAN culture.
If you're new to ASEAN, start by exploring its traditions through our permanent exhibitions. For a more in-depth knowledge of ASEAN, docent-led programs are recommended. 
The ASEAN Culture House also hosts various special exhibitions and performances. The ASEAN Culture House website is a great place to find out about upcoming exhibitions. If there's an exhibition on a topic you're interested in, you might want to visit it.
If you think you know a bit about ASEAN, it's time to experience it for yourself. Whether it's language courses to learn the languages of ASEAN countries, cultural talks and experiences to learn about traditional ASEAN food, games, costumes, and music, or cooking classes to learn how to make ASEAN dishes, there are plenty of programs to immerse yourself in ASEAN culture. 
How can you resist trying it out, especially if you're a parent eager to teach your kids about the world’s diverse cultures?
It's also a great place for teachers who want to provide their students with enriching experiences. Bring your students for an interactive docent tour and ASEAN lessons with our Group Visit Program.
Your students will gain a broader perspective with a memorable class in an exciting new setting!

item.TITLE: A house with 100 years of history
item.SUBTITLE: Ohchoryang
item.TRFC_INFO:
Use Exit 7 or Exit 9 of Choryang Station on the Busan Metro Line 1 -> Walk for 5 minutes
Parking available at the entrance of the building (free of charge)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Ohchoryang, whose name combines the exclamation “Oh!” with “Choryang” (meaning a path in the grass), is a Japanese-style wooden house built in 1925 by the Japanese architect Tanaka Hideyoshi. At that time, the only Japanese houses in the area were the Chosen Government Railway Civil Engineers’ Waiting Room and Ohchoryang, while the surrounding area was a Korean village. After liberation, the Korean entrepreneur and founder of Taechang Enterprise became the new owner and incorporated Korean cultural elements into the typical ‘Japanese enemy house’, creating a space that blends the history of modern housing and living. In 2007, the building was designated as Registered Cultural Property No. 349. Today, it is managed by the Ilmac Foundation, a subsidiary of Taechang Enterprise, and has been transformed into a multicultural space that hosts various exhibitions.
As an ‘enemy house’ that once belonged to a Japanese owner during Japanese colonial rule, Ohchoryang is an important property for researching the history of Japanese-style housing and living. However, it is also worth visiting as a cultural heritage site and complex cultural space in Busan. Thanks to the careful branding of cultural program manager Choi Sung-woo, the management of the Ilmac Foundation, and the visitors, it is becoming a place that is writing another chapter in its history.
The transformation by the Korean people's interpretation into a space with a new meaning beyond its past as an enemy-occupied house leaves a unique impression on visitors.
Respecting its identity as a 'private home', the house has been open to a limited number of guests by appointment since last year. The 100-year-old house and its various exhibits instantly transport visitors back to 1925, and it is enjoyable to find all sorts of ornaments throughout the house that would have been considered extravagant back then. The maze of corridors is a delight to navigate, with new rooms to discover, and the luxury of sipping hot tea while looking out over the gardens, which resemble a miniature forest, should not be missed.

In addition to Ohchoryang, Choryang is also home to ‘Choryang 1941’ and ‘Munhwa Gonggam Sujeong,’ which are also former enemy houses. There is also the Brown Hands Baekje Café, a modern building designated as Registered Cultural Property No. 647, making the neighborhood well worth a visit if you are exploring the area around Busan Station.

Visits are 100% appointment-based.
• Visit appointment: 30 minute-tour with a docent, free of charge
• Exhibition appointment: 1 hour 30 minutes / Exhibition + tea basket + postcard + refreshments / Chargeable
For booking, please contact us via email at ilmaclove@gmail.com.

item.TITLE: Experience Cultural Richness!
item.SUBTITLE: Busan Al-Fatih Masjid
item.TRFC_INFO:
Use Exit 8 of Dusil Station on the Busan Metro Line 1 -> Walk for 6 minutes
Parking available in front of the mosque
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
An unfamiliar structure hides among the apartment complexes: an Islamic masjid, a rare sight in Korea. 
“Masjid” means mosque, a Muslim place of worship and literally, an Islamic place of prayer.

Located in Namsan-dong, Geumjeong-gu, Busan, the Busan Al-Fatih Masjid is the second of 19 masjids opened in South Korea. Built in 1980 with the help of a Libyan benefactor, it has served as a spiritual refuge for Muslims and as a bridge for raising awareness of Islam in Korea.
The large domes and pointed minarets atop the white building are impressive.
It is said that only two Islamic masjids in Korea were built in the traditional mosque style: Seoul Central Masjid and Busan Al-Fatih Masjid.

Follow the stairs up the side of the building to the second floor, where you'll find a high-ceilinged chapel. In the center of the ceiling is the white dome you saw from outside, carved with colorful ornament including crescents and stars, symbols of Islam.
The geometric beauty of the arabesque pattern is breathtaking, and it's amazing that such an exotic landscape can be found in Busan.
The chapel is not very large, but it adheres well to the traditions of a mosque.
Features such as the mihrab, a niche in the wall indicating the direction to Mecca, the minbar, the pulpit from which the imam (prayer leader) delivers the sermon, and the separation of the men's and women's prayer rooms on the second and third floors help visitors understand the religion of Islam.

When visiting mosques, long sleeves and trousers should be worn, and access may be restricted during the JUMAH service, which takes place every Friday from 13:00 to 13:30. Please do not attend the JUMAH service to respect their culture and religion, as it is an important community service for Muslims. The mosque is open at all hours, but it is recommended to avoid visiting too early or too late.

item.TITLE: Take in the view of Busan Port at a glance from the Environmentally Friendly Skyway Observatory
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3 of Choryang Station on Busan Metro Line 1 → A 23-minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Mangyang-ro in Busan was a mountain road of refugees during the Korean War. Today, though, connected with Ibagu-gil in Choryang-dong, Dong-gu, the road winding down the mountain is a great vantage point where visitors can enjoy a panoramic view of the old downtown and the sea in front of the city. One of the unique features of this road you might find interesting is that the rooftop of some of the houses under it serves both as a parking lot and observatory.
The Environmentally Friendly Skyway Observatory located right next to Busan Science High School offers a more dramatic view of the mountain road. It’s a wooden pedestrian deck built on a mountainside covered with cherry blossoms, providing a more panoramic view from a much higher point than the mountain road. Another advantage of this deck is that it’s a safer and comfortable place to enjoy the scenery without having to worry about the cars. Climb the wooden stairs to the observatory, and you will have a panoramic view of the Busan Port Bridge across the North Port, Sinseondae Pier, Yeongdo, Nampo-dong, Jagalchi Market, and Yongdusan Park. And during the cherry blossom season in spring, the entire observatory turns into a palace of flowers.
The stunning view of Busan Port Bridge at night makes it one of the best night view spots in Busan. An exotic atmosphere is created by a row of lit houses along Mangyang-ro, the road that winds up to the mountain top.

item.TITLE: Busan's modern and contemporary history at a glance! Things to do with children in Nampo-dong
item.SUBTITLE: Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Main Building
item.ADDR1:
Main Building of Busan Modern and Contemporary History Museum, 112, Daecheong-ro, Jung-gu, Busan
No parking available (Please use a public parking lot)
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 5 of Jungang Station on the Busan Metro Line 1 -> Walk for 6 minutes
No parking
item.HLDY_INFO:
Closed on Every Monday
(The next day if Monday is a public holiday)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Do you remember the Korean household goods brand Lucky? It was created by LuckyChemical Co., Ltd., the parent company of the global conglomerate LG Group, and has been a major provider of daily essential goods since the liberation of the country. What's even more surprising is that LG's first and much-loved brand, Lucky, began in the backyard of a family home in Busan. Busan's modern and contemporary history is thus intertwined with not only Korea's great events, but also its small ones, which makes it all the more interesting. The Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum is a space where visitors can explore and experience Busan’s modern and contemporary history. The main building was renovated from the former Bank of Korea Busan Headquarters, a designated cultural property of the city, and opened earlier this year. The annex, which opened last year, is the former Dongyang Colonization Company and the American Cultural Center, both of which were symbols of colonialism during the Japanese occupation. These two historical buildings alone are worth a visit to the Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum.

Vault Art Museum

The main building in particular is notable for its use of the Bank of Korea’s old facilities. For example, the underground space that once housed the bank's vaults has been transformed into the Vault Art Museum. Viewing artworks through thick iron doors and bars designed to withstand a nuclear attack is a unique experience that can only be had at the Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum. What's more, the stylish, ever-changing lighting makes the unlit underground spaces even more secretive and mysterious. The four vaults, which have been off-limits for many years, will host the exhibition “The Original City Center, Colors of Reminiscence,” in which eight artists take a fresh look at Busan's original city center through sculpture, painting, installation, photography, and video.

Vault Art Museum

  • Address : BF1, Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Main Building, 112, Daecheong-ro, Jung-gu, Busan/li>
  • Operating Days & Hours : Tuesdays - Sundays 09:00~18:00
  • Closed Days : Every Monday (the next day if Monday is a public holiday)
  • Fee : Free
  • Inquiries : +82-51-607-8000

CASA BUSANO

On the first floor, where the Bank of Korea's customer lounge used to be, a café has been built that retains the original structure. It is an espresso café with an Italian flair, called CASA BUSANO. The ceiling with exposed pipes, the exotic interior, and the hip music attract visitors in. The café also makes full use of the history and story of the space. The signature menu includes “Bank of Korea Original Latte,” “Bank of Korea Original Padova ” “Bank of Korea Original Affogato,” and the “Gold Bar Cake,” a dessert inspired by gold bars. It is fun to discover that the vaulted room to the left of the café has been transformed into a dessert bar. Painted all yellow, the room is piled high with cakes in the shape of gold bars to delight the eyes and mouths of visitors. It's open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. and closed on the second and fourth Sundays of the month. There is no parking, but you can use the nearby Yongdusan Public Parking Lot.

CASA BUSANO

  • Address : 1F, 112, Daecheong-ro, Jung-gu, Busan
  • Operating Days & Hours : Monday - Sunday 09:00~21:00
  • Closed Days : 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Monday of every month
  • Homepage : https://www.instagram.com/casabusano/
  • Inquiries : +82-507-1339-6349

Open Cultural Space

Another vault, to the right of CASA BUSANO, has been converted into the 'Bank of Korea Archive Room'. Here you can learn about the history of the Busan Branch of the Bank of Korea and the history of the Bank of Korea's currency issuance through various historical materials. You can see the paper money issued by the Bank of Korea in the early 1900s and the first Bank of Korea banknotes produced in Japan. The souvenir shop is located behind the information desk on the first floor. You can buy a variety of products to commemorate your trip to Busan, from simple souvenirs such as stickers, postcards, and stationery, to Busan-themed coffee and alcoholic drinks, and Busan's specialty, Gijang seaweed. Also popular are key chains and mugs featuring characters from the Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum. In addition, the first floor has a variety of facilities, including a “Citizen's Convenience Facility” where you can take a break or get information about traveling in Busan, as well as a diaper changing room, a nursing room, and lockers. From the floor in front of the information desk, different colored lines indicate the location of each facility so you can follow them.

Open Cultural Space

  • Address : 1F, Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Main Building, 112, Daecheong-ro, Jung-gu, Busan
  • Operating Days & Hours : Tuesdays - Sundays 09:00~18:00
  • Closed Days : Every Monday (the next day if Monday is a public holiday)
  • Fee : Free of charge
  • Inquiries : +82-51-607-8000

Special Exhibition & Permanent Exhibition Halls

The second floor is a special exhibition hall and the third and fourth floors are permanent exhibition halls. In particular, the permanent exhibition rooms present content that reveals the history of Busan as the first port of call and the identity of Busan as a maritime capital. The first permanent exhibition room, located on the third floor, shows the time and space of Busan as it has changed since the opening of the port, from different perspectives depending on time, place, and events, under the theme of "Modern City of Busan". The modern history of Busan, the opening port city, unfolds like a movie, including the appearance of Busan where trams used to run, various objects reflecting life at that time, the changing history of Busan Port, and Busan's independence movement. The second permanent exhibition room on the 4th floor is themed 'Modern City Busan' and captures the changes that have taken place in Busan since the liberation of the country. Visitors can experience the modern history of Busan as experienced by our parents' generation, including Busan as a city for refugees, Busan in the era of industrialization symbolized by Madoros, and Busan as a hotbed of pro-democracy movements such as the April 19 Revolution and the Buma Democratic Uprising.

Special Exhibition & Permanent Exhibition Halls

  • Address : 2F, 3F, 4F, Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Main Building
  • Operating Days & Hours : Tuesdays - Sundays 09:00~18:00
  • Closed Days : Every Monday (the next day if Monday is a public holiday)
  • Fee : Free of charge
  • Inquiries : +82-51-607-8000

Children’s Experience Center

The Children's Experience Center, 'Deullaknallak', is located on the M2 floor on the east side of the main building near the Yongdusan Public Parking Lot. It offers a variety of educational and playful content such as reading, hands-on activities and English learning for children aged 5 to 8. In particular, the experience center based on Busan's modern and contemporary history, such as 'Dreaming Busan Port' where children can drive a boat, 'Epi's House' where they can try on old clothes, and 'Market Play' where they can make Gupo noodles and rice soup, provide a unique experience for children and parents alike. The center is open seven days a week from 9.30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. for 50 minutes per session and is closed on Mondays. It can only be used by booking in advance through the Busan Metropolitan Government's integrated reservation website.

Children’s Experience Center

  • Address : M2F, Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Main Building, 112, Daecheong-ro, Jung-gu, Busan
  • Operating Days & Hours : Tuesdays – Sundays 09:30~18:00
  • Closed Days : Every Monday (the next day if Monday is a public holiday)
  • Fee : Free of charge
  • Program Schedule : 09:30~10:20 / 10:30~11:20 / 11:30~12:20 / 14:00~14:50 / 15:00~15:50 / 16:00~16:50 / 17:00~17:50
  • No. of participants : Up to 30 people per session (children and parents) *Children are not allowed to enter alone (must be accompanied by a parent or guardian)
  • Note on Reservation : Only one session is available per person per day Same-day online reservation is not possible (online reservation available up to 2 days before the session) Walk-ins will be accepted only when it’s available (walk-ins may not be available if the sessions are fully booked).
  • Reservation Required : https://reserve.busan.go.kr/exprn/view?resveGroupSn=43&progrmSn=2347
  • Inquiries : +82-51-607-8000

item.TITLE: Mousai, a cultural complex for days when you want to get lost in thought
item.ADDR1: BF1, Wooshin Shopping Mall, 21, Sanseong-ro 12beon-gil, Buk-gu, Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 6, Hwamyeong Station, Busan Subway Line 2 ->5-minute walk (parking available at the shopping mall – parking ticket will be offered by Mousai)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Are you tired of the hustle and bustle of everyday life and have you shut out valuable thoughts?
On those days when you can't help but think, Mousai is the perfect place to give you food for thought.
Mousai is an independent bookstore and movie theater in Buk-gu, Busan, which stocks many independent books and art films. It also actively organizes cultural events such as reading groups and art education, fulfilling its role as a cultural complex in the neighborhood.
The name comes from Mousai, the goddess of art and learning in Greek mythology, and means 'to contemplate' in Greek, which is fitting for a space that stimulates thought with its many thought-provoking books, films and artistic gatherings.
As you walk in, you'll be greeted by a beautiful display of zero-waste products. The products are full of Mousai's own personality and show the "Mousai”-ness that makes you think twice about the environment. Just past the zero-waste stalls is a café where you can soak up the atmosphere over a drink - not just coffee and juice, but also beer and wine too. It's perfect for those who want to soak up the atmosphere of books and movies over a drink. 
There is also a theater in Mousai that shows independent films. It regularly shows independent short films that have unfortunately missed out on theatrical release, and in addition to regular screenings, it also shows a number of good films through special screenings. It's always open, even when it's not showing movies, so you can always drop in for a good read after buying a book.
The theater can also be rented for community cultural activities. In addition to the theater you can also rent community meeting room!
Whether you want to reacquaint yourself with books and moviesaven't seen in a while, or build a cultural community with friends and like-minded people, Mousai, an inspiring independent bookstore and movie theater, is the place to be!

item.MAIN_TITLE: 부산 트래블라운지 (한, 영, 중간, 중번, 일)
item.TITLE: True Busan Experience Programs, Put together by the Busan Travel Lounge
item.SUBTITLE: Busan Travel Lounge
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1 of Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → 2-min walk (Paid parking available at Chinatown Public Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The first place that greets visitors to Busan is the Busan Travel Lounge, the refuge area for tourists in Busan. Busan Travel Lounge offers immaculately organized facilities and a suite of experience programs related to Busan. Let’s take a look at what Busan Travel Lounge is all about and what exciting programs they have in store for you!

Busan Travel Lounge

Busan Travel Lounge is a tourist cultural space that draws a large crowd of visitors thanks to its location across Busan Station. In addition to providing a much-needed rest area for travelers tired of moving, the lounge also has an information desk that details Busan’s tourist attractions, a storage room for people on foot to store their heavy luggage, and other facilities that cater to the convenience of tourists. Busan Travel Lounge also provides optimal services for all visitors to Busan, such as free meeting room rental and charging. The cute interior featuring Busan’s mascot, Boogi, and its landmark Gwangandaegyo Bridge, as well as flight departure timetables, are also a highlight of this place. The true strength of Busan Travel Lounge, however, lies in the variety of tour programs offered to the visitors every weekend.

1. Indoor One-day Classes

2. Thematic Busan Old City Center Tour Programs

3. Seasonal Busan Cultural Experiences

Let’s then take a look at what interesting programs await us!

Indoor One-day Classes

Sometimes, you end up with gaps in your schedule. If you have an hour to spare, drop by the Busan Travel Lounge and take the one-day classes there! Busan Travel Lounge offers one-day craft classes every weekend. Some of them are themed after Busan’s tourist sites, like the Busan Gwangalli Beach Cake-making and Busan Sea Mint Soap-making. In addition to cakes and soaps, the lounge offers a variety of crafting classes, including resin art, shrinkles, rattan, suncatchers, candles, knitting, coffee classes, ceramics, pop art, and more. In fact, these programs are worth setting aside some time in your schedule! The classes’ themes differ on a weekly basis, so if you're interested, be sure to check out Busan Travel Lounge's Instagram and Naver Smart Store pages before making a reservation. Note that tourists will be given priority in reservation, as the space explicitly caters to tourists!

Busan Preference Tour

One of the nicest moments in traveling is discovering a new taste for something you were unaware of before. In “Busan Preference Tour,” you can discover your new preferences as you explore the different parts of the city! Busan Travel Lounge offers seasonal tours that are themed after the different spaces in Busan and the preferences one can pursue in the city.

Preference for Film Cameras: Record Your Busan

For instance, “Preference for Film Cameras: Record Your Busan” program introduces you to the analog aesthetics of film cameras in the equally analog spaces of Busan’s old city center and its alleyways. The tour has two routes corresponding to the Dong-gu and Jung-gu Districts of the city. Both routes bring to life the charms of the two spaces, so you can take some really nice pictures in the program. Even if you are not familiar with film camera photography, don’t worry; the program includes a disposable film camera with more than 24 shots available and a simple tutorial for using film cameras.

Start from Busan Travel Lounge – Chinatown Street (Texas Street) – (former) Baekje Hospital – 168 Stairs – Ibagu Skyway Observatory

The Dong-gu Route starts at Busan Station, the heart of Busan’s transit system, and begins with a multicultural experience at Busan’s Chinatown. Then, the tour brings you to Ibagu-gil Road, which exemplifies Busan’s modern and contemporary history, leading to a panoramic view of Busan Port. How’s that for a thorough tour of Dong-gu District’s scenery and culture? Get your camera ready because you will be taking a lot of pictures on the tour!

Start from Busan Tourist Information Center – Yeongdodaegyo Wharf – Yongdusan Park – Gukje Market – Bosu Book Street

In the Jung-gu Route, you will explore the unique spots that speak to the lives of the people of Busan, such as the Yeongdodaegyo Wharf, Yongdusan Park, Gukje Market, and Bosu Book Street. As you record the alleyways and historic sites, which have witnessed the city’s growth, with a film camera, you will find that you have grown much closer to Busan. The Preference Tour offers different thematic tours according to the season, so make sure to follow the Busan Travel Lounge Instagram account and the Naver Smart Store page for updates. Alternatively, just jump into the first Preference Tour you encounter during your trip in Busan and discover a new taste for yourself!

Busan Old City Center Trekking Snap Tour

Trekking and snapshots at the same time! In the Busan Old City Center Trekking Snap Tour, you walk the city with a snap photography expert to discover the hidden alleyways of this charming city and record your visit through pictures. Because these tours are overseen by experts, you are sure to get a quality picture for your album. What’s more, you will get your pictures in both original and edited versions! This tour is likewise divided into two routes, one in the Jung-gu District and the other in the Nam-gu District. The itinerary and the sites you visit are identical to those in the Preference Tour, so refer to the information on Busan Preference Tours for more information!

Start from Busan Travel Lounge – Chinatown Street (Texas Street) – (former) Baekje Hospital – 168 Stairs – Ibagu Skyway Observatory

Start from Busan Tourist Information Center – Yeongdodaegyo Wharf – Yongdusan Park – Gukje Market – Bosu Book Street

One of the best sceneries in the scenic old city center of Busan can be found at the Sanbok Road. If you want to build a healthy body and an imaginative mind at the same time, sign up for this tour!

Dong-gu Route

Jung-gu Route

Seasonal Busan Cultural Experiences

Once you’ve toured the major tourist sites of Busan, it’s time to experience the life of Busan citizens. The Busan Travel Lounge operates a program where you can discover the culture of Busan citizens by season and experience the culture by living as a Busan citizen for a day. Go to a baseball game and sing and cheer with the crowd in the “Baseball Culture Experience” or take part in the “Yacht Tour” for a dynamic experience of Busan’s seas. Many “Seasonal Busan Cultural Experiences” await you in the future as well, so look forward to it! Busan Travel Lounge information: Go to

item.TITLE: Banyeo Chorok Park, a Child-friendly Forest Playground & Valley
item.SUBTITLE: Banyeo Chorok Park & Jangsan Valley
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Busan Wondong Station, Busan-Donghae Line → Bus No. 44, 52 or 144 from Busan Wondong Station → 8-minute walk from Ilshin Bus Final Station (Parking: Banyeo Library Public Parking Lot)
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME: Chorok Park Roller Slide: 09:00 – 17:00, 7 Days a Week
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Spend the rest of your summer cooling off at Banyeo Chorok Park & Jangsan Valley, where kids can play with nature!
Banyeo Chorok Park is especially popular with families, offering a variety of facilities at the Banyeo Recreational Green Space, including a picnic area, a net playground, and a barefoot loess path. Both children and adults can enjoy interacting with nature. To access these facilities and the valley, you'll have to climb a fairly steep path, making it a great place for both fun and a healthy exercise.

The main attraction here is the 43-meter long roller slide, the longest in Busan, offering an exhilarating experience for children. Safety rules are clearly posted, so as long as you follow them, you can enjoy the ride safely. At the end of the slide, you'll find a net playground where toddlers can swing and play, as well as hammocks and wooden chairs for adults to relax in.


Right next to the Recreational Green Space is a shallow stream that's great for wading and playing in, and full of small fish that children will love to catch. Just remember: Release your catch back into the stream!

item.TITLE: Refresh your mind with the clean air and water of Daeshin Park & Daeshin Valley (Former)
item.SUBTITLE: Jungang Park (formerly Daeshin Park) Daeshin Valley
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 4, Seodaeshin Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. Seo-gu 5 at Seodaeshin Station → 6-minute walk from Dong-a University Hospital Station, Daeshin Park Public Parking Lot (charged)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Experience the rejuvenating power of nature at Jungang Park (formerly Daeshin Park) and Daeshin Valley—a tranquil inner-city oasis filled with refreshing phytoncides to revitalize your spirit! 

The former Daeshin Park is conveniently located near Dong-A University Hospital and is easily accessible. The park's main attraction is its cypress forest, where you can enjoy the fresh air immediately upon arrival. Well-maintained walking paths wind through the forest, making it easy for visitors to take a leisurely walk. The park also offers various amenities for both residents and tourists, including a flat area for jogging and playing badminton, resting benches, a mineral spring, and basic exercise equipment.

It used to supply drinking water to the Busan area. There are two water sources in Daeshin Park. The first, located near the cypress forest and Daeshin Valley, has been turned into a lake where you can see carp, soft-shelled turtles, and other creatures.

Nestled near a cypress forest, Daeshin Valey offers shallow water that reaches a child’s knees, making it perfect for splashing around and cooling off. The stream is teeming with small fish and marsh snails that children can collect and play with, providing a wonderful opportunity for children to connect with nature. Just be sure to release your catch back into the stream to help preserve the natural environment!

item.TITLE: Auto camping in Gudeok Valley, a perfect getaway to a hidden natural spot
item.SUBTITLE: Gudeok Camping Site Valley
item.ADDR1: Gudeok Youth Training Center, 109, Kkonmaeul-ro 156beon-gil, Seo-gu, Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 4, Seodaeshin Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. Seo-gu 1 at Seodaeshin Station → 4-minute walk from Gudeok Kkonmaeul Station (Parking: Gudeok Kkonmaeul Public Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Discover a hidden gem known only to Busan locals! 
Take the kids to a peaceful valley near Gudeok Camping Site for a relaxing getaway.


Gudeok Camping Site is located next to the former Daeshin Park. If you follow the walking trail that starts at Daeshin Park, you'll discover a beautiful natural area. The most notable nearby attraction is Naewonjeongsa Temple, which is famous for its temple stay program and is the largest temple near the city center. It's a fantastic place to explore and connect with nature.

Since this area supplies drinking water, you’ll notice several large water sources. Near Gudeok, you'll find the 'second water source,' where you can see carp and other aquatic life, as well as a fountain that operates at different times throughout the day. There is also a sports field near the campsite where you can enjoy a quick game of football.



The stream that runs around the campsite is shallow enough for children to splash around in, making it a great place to cool off with a dip in the summer.

item.TITLE: Beomeosa Temple in Yongseong Valley, where you can get a glimpse of Busan's history and enjoy the cool valley stream
item.SUBTITLE: Beomeosa Yongseong Valley
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Nopo Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 90 at Beomeosa Ipgu Station → 2-minute walk from Beomeosa Parking Lot Station (Parking: Beomeosa Public Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Do you know Yosan Kim Jeonghan, a key figure in Busan's literary history? The reservoir depicted in Yosan's work Sahachon is actually Beomeosa Yongseong Dam. So Yongseong Dam is not only a reservoir in the heart of the city, but also a place of literary significance.

Yongseong Valley has a stream that flows from Yongseong Dam, creating a stunning waterfall that is sure to refresh your mind. However, as shown in the photo, the water upstream from the dam is very powerful, making it unsafe to enter the waterfall.



Consider exploring the valley, where the water is only knee-deep, making it safe for young children to play. The area is also home to many small fish, making it an excellent place to learn about ecology. Nearby, you’ll find a walking trail called Nuri-gil and a rest area, perfect for combining water play with a leisurely walk.

Visit Yongseong Valley for a blend of Busan's history refreshing stream!

item.TITLE: Yongso Well-Being Park, A Hidden Walk in the Heart of the City
item.SUBTITLE: Yongso Well-Being Park
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Gijang Station, Busan-Donghae Line → Bus No. Gijang-gun 11 from Gijang Catholic Church Station → 13-minute walk from Seobu Jugong Apt. Station
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Surrounded by beautiful natural scenery, this is one of the best hidden hikes to enjoy the forest trails and Yongsogol Reservoir in all four seasons.  
Smell the relaxing seasonal scent with a gentle breeze from the reservoir. You'll experience a different side of Gijang on this walk.

Take the kids out on the weekends and keep fit with a walk on the beautiful waterfront deck.

Yongso Well-Being Park is a great place for walks for all ages, from toddlers to the elderly.
It is especially recommended for families.

item.TITLE: Explore the Sounds of Korea, Gugak Experience Hall, Busan National Gugak Center
item.SUBTITLE: Gugak Experience Hall, Busan National Gugak Center
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5, Yangjeong Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 179 or No. 63 from Baekjo Apt. Station → 5-minute walk from Busan Citizens Park (Parking at Busan National Gugak Center)
item.ITEMCNTNTS: Think Gugak is difficult to learn? Now it's easy and fun to learn at the Gugak Experience Hall, Busan National Gugak Center! The Gugak Experience Hall opened in October 2023. Unlike the Busan National Gugak Center, which focus mostly on performances, the Gugak Experience Hall offers various experiences and exhibitions that bring you closer to traditional Korean music. When you first enter the center, you’ll see the outdoor performance stage. This is where you can enjoy exciting Gugak performances, many of which are free. In addition to the outdoor stage, there is also an indoor performance hall that hosts a variety of shows. To make the most of your visit, it is a good idea to check the the Busan National Gugak Center’s performance schedule on their website before visiting the center. ▷Shortcut to the website Inside the Experience Hall, you will find exhibits related to gugak. The first floor is an immersive media art room where you can enjoy the coolness of gugak through colorful gugak media art. The digital data exhibition room on the 1st and 2nd floors is a place where you can learn things you didn't know about gugak, and various archival materials are displayed to pique your curiosity. The immersive exhibition room on the second floor is a space where you can experience Korean musical instruments through digital devices, which is especially attractive to visitors with children. Right next door is a children's experience room where they can make paper art of the janggu, an hourglass-shaped Korean drum and the taepyeongso, or traditional wind instrument, which is a great way for them to experience Korean music. There are also plenty of resting areas throughout the center, so you can take a break after enjoying a performance or exhibition. The Gugak Experience Hall is located right in front of Busan Citizens Park, so it's a great place to end your day with a leisurely stroll in the park afterwards. Spend an enriching day at the Gugak Experience Hall, where you can experience the beauty of Korean music with a modern twist!

item.TITLE: Don’t give up on math! Go to ‘Busan Mathematics Culture Museum’, a hands-on math playground
item.SUBTITLE: Busan Mathematics Culture Museum
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3, Buam Station, Busan Metro Line 2 -> 2-minute walk (Busan Mathematics Culture Museum Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Math can be fun at the Busan Mathematics Culture Museum. Explore the exciting world of mathematics at the Busan Mathematics Culture Center, the world's largest math culture space. The Busan Mathematics Culture Museum was opened to spread the joy of mathematics to people, and it holds various exhibitions and experience programs to popularize mathematics among the public. The museum is spread over five floors, so there are many different things to explore on each floor. After registering for the experience programs in the lobby on the B1-1st floor, go up to the second floor where the full-blown math experience programs begin.

2F : Mathematics Play Hall & Mathematics Library

3F : Career Exploration Hall & Media Hall

4층 : Subject Experience Hall & History and Wisdom Hall

5F : Board Game Hall

The Mathematics Play Hall on the second floor is a playful place to explore math. It's filled with hands-on, interactive programs that bring math to life, whether you're trying to figure out the size of a pizza slice or building your own da Vinci Dome. It's great for toddlers and early elementary students who are new to math. The Mathematics Library, located on the same floor, has math-related books to help you explore math in more depth. The Subject Experience Hall on the fourth floor is organized around the theme of math in textbooks, making it more fun for elementary and middle school students and up who are starting to learn math in school. The History and Wisdom Hall on the same floor displays math in human history, so check it out if you're interested in learning more about the history of math. When you're done, you can spend some time with your kids playing fun board games in the Board Game Hall on the fifth floor. Also on the third floor is the Career Exploration Hall, where you can learn about how math is used in different careers, and the Media Hall, where you can watch math videos. You can enter the Busan Mathematics Culture Museum by reservation or on the spot. If there are many visitors, you may not be allowed to enter, so it is recommended to make a reservation.

item.TITLE: Busan's First Buddhist Temple: Mahasa Temple
item.SUBTITLE: Mahasa Temple
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 4, Yangjeong Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. 20, 62 or 57 from Exit 4, Yangjeong Station -> Transfer to Bus no. Yeonje-gu 2 from Shin-ri Samgeori -> 8-minute walk from Mahasa Station (Parking at Café EL 16.52)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
As you slowly climb the forest trail at Bongsu-ro in Yeonje-gu, Busan, 
you'll come across a hospitality banner and a Buddha statue that greets you with a bright smile.

Mahasa is a temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism that was first built during the Silla Dynasty, making it one of the first temples in Busan. The temple was burned down during the Imjin War, or the Japanese Invasions of Korea in 1592, but was gradually rebuilt throughout the 18th and 19th centuries.
The wellness program is updated each year, with experiences such as meditation, temple food therapy, and more to balance physical, mental, and social health in the serene, deep mountains.
When you feel so frustrating and disturbed,
When you want wisdom and compassion to fill you up, 
why not spend some time inhaling and exhaling in Mahasa Temple?

Coming down the mountain path while listening to the sound of a bell at Mahasa Temple, one of the Eight Scenic Views in Suyeong-gu, will be another special memory.

item.TITLE: Ibagu-gil Photo Studio To Capture Memories
item.SUBTITLE: Ibagu-gil Photo Studio
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 7, Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 – One minute of walk ( Public parking is available nearby)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Ibagu-gil Photo Studio brings a sense of nostalgia with its old building and wooden sign. The place feels like it’s been around forever, but surprisingly, it's only recently opened.

The interior of the photo studio features a mix of vintage props that creates a warm and cozy atmosphere. A large teddy bear and brown furniture add to the mellow vibe of the photos here.

The studio specializes in black-and-white photography and offers a wide range of photography types, including family, couples, weddings, and portraits. The owner is an experienced photographer, ensuring that your photos will be perfect for your purposes. Every detail carefully, from the layout to background and prop placement, is carefully thought out, so your photos will turn out beautifully.
They also offer photo restoration services, so if you have old, blurry or faded photos, this is the perfect place to bring them back to life.


Ibagu-gil Photo Studio is a member store of Ibagu Pay, so you can earn incentive rewards when you use Ibagu Pay, making it even more affordable.
If you have a special occasion you don’t want to miss and want to capture it with a professional photographer, Ibagu-gil Photo Studio is the perfect choice!

item.TITLE: North Port Waterfront Park, an up-and-coming night spot in Busan
item.SUBTITLE: North Port Waterfront Park
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 6, Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 – 15-minute walk (Busan Port Outdoor Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The sea meets futuristic landscaping in the heart of the city. Enjoy a special evening stroll at North Port Waterfront Park!

The North Port Waterfront Park is a waterfront park developed as part of the the North Port Redevelopment Project. It’s also a downtown park, easily accessible by getting off at Busan Station and walking across the pedestrian bridge. The park’s vibrant lights and futuristic design make it an attractive new spot for enjoying Busan’s nighttime views.
The park is well lit, making it a great place for a relaxing walk at night. It is also spacious with a well-maintained path, perfect for running or taking the kids or dog for an evening out.
Though it’s best known as a nighttime walking spot thanks to the beautiful night view of the Busanhangdaegyo Bridge in the background, you can also enjoy the lush pampas grass along the promenade during the day.

The North Port Waterfront Park features multi-purpose plazas, lawns, ground fountains, decks and more to create a more fulfilling experience for visitors. With beautiful landscaping that blends naturally into the urban environment, it’s a great place to enjoy an evening.

item.TITLE: Perfect Promotion with Ocean View! Busan North Port Redevelopment Promotion Hall
item.SUBTITLE: Busan North Port Redevelopment Promotion Hall
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 6, Choryang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 ->19-minute walk (Busan Port International Passenger Terminal parking lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Let’s learn more about the Busan North Port Redevelopment Promotion Hall, where you can enjoy a panoramic view of the sea and get a glimpse of the future of North Port!

Bukhang, or North Port, is gaining attention as Korea’s first port redevelopment project. The Busan North Port Redevelopment Promotion Hall is a space created to help visitors learn more about the project. Conveniently located near Busan Station, it’s situated within the Busan Port International Passenger Terminal for easy access.

The first thing you’ll notice is the breezy ocean view overlooking the North Port. The view alone is reason enough to come, but the comfortable interior and cozy seating make it even better.

The diorama showing the redevelopment of the North Port is also worth mentioning. You can also see the redevelopment vision in the promotional video! 

In addition to the redevelopment, you can learn about the history of Busan Port, making it a great place to explore both the past and future of the North Port.
If you want to catch a glimpse of the future of the North Port, which will become the heart of Busan with the upcoming changes, this is the place to be!

item.TITLE: Culture and Arts Platform, where everyone is an artist
item.SUBTITLE: Culture and Arts Platform
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3, Gupo Station, Busan Metro Line 3 → 4-minuate walk (Culture and Arts Platform parking lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Spend an artistic day at Buk-gu’s Culture and Arts Platform, where the spirit of culture and art is alive and well! 

The Culture and Arts Platform offers a variety of different art experience programs and exhibitions. In the lobby, you'll find charming handicrafts and unique pieces created by students. Some some of these unique handicrafts are available for purchase, and you’re sure to find something that grabs your attention as soon as you walk in.

On the first floor, you can take part in a variety of arts and crafts activities like writing, painting, ceramics, wood carving and more. Whether you’re a child who loves creating things or an adult with a passion for art, there's something for everyone.
The second floor has a lecture hall where various special lectures are held. The hands-on program and lecture schedules vary, so it’s a good idea to call ahead for details. 


The Manse Gallery, located on the third floor, hosts exhibitions with a different theme each time. The exhibitions are not only about art, but also about history and culture, which makes them even more meaningful.

If you're looking for a more intimate encounter with art and culture, check out the Culture and Arts Platform, a space where everyone can unleash their artistic side!

item.TITLE: ‘Bookdoochilseong Library’, where books meet people and become a light and a guide
item.SUBTITLE: Bookdoochilseong Library
item.ADDR1: 1F, Bldg. B, Hyupsung Marina G7, 160, Chungjang-daero, Dong-gu, Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 6, Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> 13-minute walk
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME: 10:00 a.m. - 8:00 p.m. on Weekdays / 10:00 a.m. - 8:00 p.m. on Weekends
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
With the slogan “A place where books meet people and become a light and a guide," The Bookdoochilseong Library in Busan’s North Port immediately grabs attention with its towering stacks of books reaching the ceiling, cascading bookshelves, and Chaekoreum Plaza, where you can enjoy movies and performances.

The Bookdoochilseong Library is emerging as a new cultural complex and landmark in North Port, offering a diverse and creative cultural space that includes an academic center, cafe, and performance venue.
The library is divided into seven rooms, inspired by the motif of the Big Dipper constellation, with books arranged by theme and subject, making it easy for everyone to find something to read. The cozy and comfortable interior, where you can sit anywhere, inspires a desire to read.

The Bookdoocillseong Library is also known as a place to experience art and culture through various programs, such as the ‘Dodam Dodam Academy’, which fosters children's creativity, the ‘Sunset Concert’, which captures the romantic vibes of the sunset through musical performances, and ‘Single Men and Women's Love Story’, which explores the theme of love through reading and conversation. If you are interested, why not join one of them!

item.TITLE: Songjeong Gudeokpo-gil: A Hidden Gem in Haeundae
item.SUBTITLE: Songjeong Gudeokpo-gil
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 2, Songjeong Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line → Bus No. 185 from Songjeong Station → 11-minute walk from KT Songjeong Tower Station (parking at Songjeong Beach public parking lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Looking for an escape from the hustle and bustle of the city? Check out Haeundae's hidden gem, Gudeokpo-gil!

Gudeokpo-gil is a colorful walkway atop the breakwater. Compared to other spots in Haeundae, it attracts fewer tourists, making it a more secluded place to relax. The trails are well-maintained, and you’ll often see people walking their dogs or enjoying low-intensity trekking. Each section features unique painted patterns, adding a bit of fun to your walk.

Telescopes and benches are also available in certain sections. Take a closer look at the ocean through a telescope, or sit on a bench and enjoy the view of the Songjeong Sea. The crystal-clear water makes it a perfect spot for a weekend getaway with your loved ones or family.

There are also many cafes along Gudeokpo-gil, making it the perfect spot to enjoy a coffee with a stunning view of the sea. If you need a break after a long walk, why not relax with a cup of coffee at one of the nearby cafes? Whether you’re looking for a quick rest or want to enjoy a special day with your friends, significant other, or family, Gudeokpo-gil is the place to be!

item.TITLE: Sanbok Road Exhibition Hall in Mangyang-ro: Showcasing the History of the Hillside Road
item.SUBTITLE: Sanbok Road Exhibition Hall in Mangyang-ro
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5, Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 508 or No. 190 from Busan Station → 3-minute walk from Dongil Park Mansion Station (Parking available at Sanbok Road Exbition Hall)
item.ITEMCNTNTS: The Sanbok Road Exhibition Hall on Mangyang-ro is a unique place where you can experience Busan's history and culture. The Archive Zone is divided into 10 themes, summarizing the history of Busan’s Dong-gu district from the Japanese occupation to the Korean War. One of the themes, "Gadaegi” (a technique for carrying heavy loads with a hook on one’s shoulder), explores the lives and history of workers, while also showcasing panoramas depicting evacuees’ lives and disappearing natural landscape. In the Play Zone, visitors can listen to stories about the people of Sanbok Road and build model houses, while in the Souvenir Experience Zone, visitors can decorate postcards with stamps and photos. Don’t forget to capture the beautiful views of Busan Port and Jung-gu at the stunning Photo Zone in the exhibition center.

item.TITLE: “Dakbatgol Mural Village”: A Harmony of Colors
item.SUBTITLE: Dakbatgol Mural Village
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5, Dongdaeshin Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → 18-minute walk
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME: Stairs of Wishes Monorail : 07:30~20:00 on weekdays, 10:00~17:30 on weekends
item.ITEMCNTNTS: Dakbatgol Mural Village, a vibrant community adorned with six different themes, was created in 2010 by artist Gu Bon-ho and residents who settled there after the 1953 Busan Station Fire. The village's Stairs of Wishes, with its 192 steps, is said to be the place where wishes come true. Adding to the village’s charm, there's also a cute monorail for residents.

item.TITLE: Daecheong Sky Observatory: A Viewpoint Over Busan
item.SUBTITLE: Daecheong Sky Observatory
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 7, Jungang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 86 or No. 186 from SC Cheil Bank Station → 9-minute walk from Busan Digital High School
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Daecheong Sky Observatory is located next to Color Village.
From here, you can enjoy a breathtaking night view of Busanhangdaegyo Bridge, Borgesian Mountain, Busan Tower and Namhangdaegyo Bridge.
As you take in the colorful lights of the night, take a moment to reflect on how the mountainside road has transformed into the beautiful place it is today. 
And be sure to remember the vibrant colors shining through the alleys for a long time.

item.TITLE: ‘Color Village’ in Mangyang-ro, Full of Vibrant Colors
item.SUBTITLE: Color Village
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 17, Jungang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 86 or No. 186 from SC Cheil Bank Station → 1-minute walk from Busan Digital High School (Parking available at Daecheong Public Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS: Color Village is a charming tourist spot along a pretty street lined with colorful murals on the walls of old houses, inviting visitors to take their time and enjoy the view. Created in 2009 as part of Busan City's Color Landscape Plan, the area has a quiet, peaceful atmosphere. The orange monorail runs uphill through the village, and the cute murals and decorations along the way make the strenuous climb worthwhile.

item.TITLE: Music Complex Seoul – Busan: Indulge in 20,000 LPs!
item.SUBTITLE: Music Complex Seoul - Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, OSIRIA Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line -> 12-minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Introducing Music Complex Seoul – Busan: A Special Destination for Vinyl Lovers!
Music Complex Seoul - Busan is known for its red lighting and distinctive high floor. It’s also famous for housing over 20,000 vinyl records, with a wide variety of albums catering to diverse musical tastes. One of its main attractions is that, for an admission fee of 20,000 won per person, you can enjoy unlimited music listening.
On the first floor, you can order drinks and sit down to enjoy vinyl. Each table is equipped with its own turntable and headset, but using the equipment can be a bit tricky depending on the turntable’s features. If you’re unsure, don’t hesitate to ask the staff for help. Also, there are separate LPs for listening and for sale, which can be confusing, so be sure to read the descriptions carefully before making your choice!

On the stairs between the first and second floors, you’ll find a decorative cabinet filled with LP albums, which is also famous as a photo zone due to its unique interior design at Music Complex Seoul - Busan. There is also a DJ booth concept photo zone with an LP album cabinet backdrop. Capture stunning photos in this special photo zone, a feature that you can only find here.
The second floor features a venue for live music performances. Jazz, Latin music, and other genres are performed here. You can check their Instagram page (@music.complex.seoul) for the schedule and more information.
Spend a day indulging your ears at Music Complex Seoul - Busan, where you can relax and enjoy vinyl music in a laid-back atmosphere.

item.TITLE: Nurimaru APEC House for a night walk with stunning night views
item.SUBTITLE: Nurimaru APEC House
item.ADDR1: Nurimaru APEC House, 116 Dongbaek-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Dongbaek Station, Busan Metro Line 2 → 14-minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Dongbaekseom Island is another popular spot of Busan with a beautiful night view. The cityscape creating harmony with nature is truly remarkable.
The famous Nurimaru APEC House is located in Dongbaekseom Island. At night, this circular building lights up and presents a beautiful view alongside the sparkling Gwangandaegyo Bridge. The Lighthouse Plaza is inside Dongbaekseom Island. From the Lighthouse Plaza, the view of the Nurimaru APEC House, the ocean, and Gwangandaegyo Bridge create a harmonious scene.
As Dongbaekseom Island is surrounded by the ocean, seeing the night view from the Lighthouse Plaza is a special experience. The dark sky and ocean surround Dongbaekseom Island, while the colorful and gleaming Nuri Village and the beautiful Gwangandaegyo Bridge with its flamboyance are similar to jewels embedded in a black curtain.

Listen to the sound of waves splashing against the rocks while looking at the beautiful night view of Busan from Dongbaekseom Island Lighthouse Plaza truly relaxes the mind.


A 10-minute walk from APEC House will take you to APEC Naru Park, which was built to commemorate the APEC Summit. It is recommended that you visit it as it is large, with well-maintained walking paths and various sculptures, making it a great place to take a stroll and see the sights.

item.TITLE: Yongho Starlight Park, a special place to stroll!
item.SUBTITLE: Yongho Starlight Park
item.CNTCT_TEL:
Management Office: +82-51-607-4048
Exhibition Center : +82-51-607-4050
Office In Charge : +82-51-607-5611
item.TRFC_INFO: 2-minute walk from Kyungsung Univ. · Pukyong Nat'l Univ. Station , Busan Metro Line 2 -> Bus No. Nam-gu 2 from Kyungsung University Entrance -> Get off at Bunpo High School-> 8-minute walk (No parking available. Use public parking at Yongho Bay Cruise Terminal)
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME: Everyday 09:00~22:00 (For Exhibition Center, 13:00 – 21:00, Closed on Mondays and Tuesdays)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Why not enjoy a nighttime stroll at Yongho Starlight Park, a former pier that has been transformed into an iconic viewpoint of Busan’s Gwangan Bridge?

Do you remember the 2019 incident when a Russian cargo ship collided with the Gwangandaegyo Bridge? The collision happened at Yongho Pier, which was closed afterward and has since been reestablished as Yongho Starlight Park.

As you stroll through the park after sunset, lights sparkle like fireflies underfoot, making it a delightful walk for both kids and adults. The photo zone at the entrance is ideal for couples and families, and the view of the illuminated Gwangandaegyo Bridge and Haeundae makes this one of Busan's most popular night spots.
Located within the park, the Exhibition Center features a permanent exhibition hall, a media arts zone, viewing and resting areas, and amenities like a library for both adults and children, making it a great place to learn and relax.
Looking for a romantic date spot or a place to stroll with family or pets?
Yongho Starlight Park is perfect for a walk to welcome the changing season!
It's a spot where you can enjoy nature right in the heart of the city.

item.TITLE: Busan Workation Central Center: A Mecca for Workationers
item.SUBTITLE: Busan Workation Central Center
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 6, Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> 5-minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Busan is a great place to work, live, and play – and you can even do all three at once!

The 'Busan Workation Central Center' is the go-to spot for workationers visiting Busan. As the largest base center among workcation offices, it's the ideal place to get work done.

The center offers a range of independent workspaces for solo workationers, as well as meeting rooms for corporate teams. There's even a couch for a quick break, and basic facilities like a break room and lockers are well-maintained. 
Another great feature is the view of the sea near Busan Port and the city skyline. The window view provides the perfect mental break when you're feeling stuck.

No discussion of the Busan Workation Central Center would be complete without mentioning its networking program. Here, you can hear from local brand builders, creative content creators, and pioneering entrepreneurs in the IT industry.
If you're considering starting a business or running a company, be sure to check out the valuable business lectures on offer.

item.TITLE: The Hyuil X Desker Workation Center: Where work meets relaxation!
item.SUBTITLE: The Hyuil X Desker Workation Center
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 8, Nampo Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. Yeongdo-gu 5 from Yeongdodaegyo Bridge·Nampo Station -> 7-minute walk from Bongnae Market Station
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Work feels like a holiday with sea views!
Check out The Hyuil X Desker Workation Center, a workcation mecca where the sea surrounds you.

The Hyuil X Desker Workcation Center is a Busan workcation satellite located in Yeongdo, Busan.
