As the name suggests, it’s a collaborative space by workcation brand 'The Hyuil' and office furniture brand 'Desker.’ The center is perfectly configured for productivity, featuring high-quality furniture for comfort. Plus, every corner offers a refreshing sea view of Busan Port – ideal for clearing your head.

While other workation centers offer a free and open atmosphere, this one leans more towards an office feel, putting the emphasis on 'work' rather than 'relaxation.’ The space is divided into co-working areas, seminar rooms for meetings, and individual cubicle seating, making it versatile for various needs. The center is also fully equipped with wireless internet, dual monitors, beam projectors, power banks, and all the essential equipment to get work done.

When you need a break, explore the famous cafes and select shops right in the same building. The Hyuil X Desker Workation Center combines high efficiency with fun and relaxation, offering the perfect workation experience!

item.TITLE: See Sea With BOOK:  A tranquil place to work and unwind, offering a fantastic view of the ocean around Yeongdo Island.
item.SUBTITLE: See Sea with BOOK
item.ADDR1: See Sea with BOOK bookstore, 99, Huinnyeoul-gil, Yeongdo-gu, Busan
item.TRFC_INFO: 1-minute walk from Exit, Nampo Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. 5 from Yeongdodaegyo Bridge Nampo Station -> Get off at Huinnyeoul Culture Village Station -> 5-minute walk (No parking)
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME:
Monday–Saturday 07:00–22:00 
(Operated as an unmanned bookstore outside the hours of 11:00–18:00)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Check out See See With BOOK, a bookstore with a laid-back atmosphere where you can relax, ready, or work while enjoying a view of Yeongdo's blue ocean.

The book curation space spans three floors and a rooftop, each featuring different categories. It's a great place to browse and pick your favorite books, offering a relaxing break from work whenever you need it. Feel free to read as much as you like, and you can also purchase books on the spot.
It's also a relief not to have to worry about background noise while working or reading. You pay by the hour, and you can enter via QR code - unlike most bookstores - so you won’t be disturbed by people coming and going. A complimentary welcome tea adds to the perfect combination of tea, ocean view, and a book. For added comfort, you can also visit the café next door, Yeoulmarq.
It's worth noting that See Sea With BOOK is also a satellite Workation center, offering Workation visitors free space rental and coffee – fantastic deal! 
With so many reasons to visit, See Sea With BOOK is an ideal place to work and unwind simultaneously!

item.TITLE: Pathfinder Nampo Branch: Discovering a new way together
item.SUBTITLE: Pathfinder Nampo Branch
item.TRFC_INFO: 2-minute walk from Exit 7, Jungang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. 81 or 40 from SC Cheil Bank Station -> Get off at Gukje Market Station -> 5-minute walk (No parking)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Discovering a new way together!
Check out Pathfinder Nampo Branch, a shared office and Busan Workation satellite center for those looking to combine work and relaxation.

Pathfinder Nampo is conveniently located in the heart of Nampo-dong, making it an ideal spot for a quick break and to explore some of the city's main attractions, like Yongdusan Park and Bupyeong Kkangtong Market.
When you arrive, just check in at Mars Coffee Lab on the second floor, where you’ll receive a QR code for access. As a workcation participant, you'll enjoy a complimentary Americano or latte on your first visit - a perfect boost to kickstart your workday!

In addition to its convenient location, the coworking space has everything from private, one-person areas for focused work to open meeting rooms that can be used for team collaboration. It's the perfect place to work together as a team. Visitors from outside the office are welcome to stay for an hour, and there are plenty of other useful amenities, like printers. For more info, just scan the QR code.

On the third floor, you’ll find a vibrant cultural space called the 'Corner Theatre' - a perfect spot to take a break from work. As mentioned, there are plenty of nearby attractions, like BIFF Square and Bosu-dong Book Street, ideal for unwinding after a productive day. 
Why not enjoy an enriching workation experience at Pathfinder Nampo Branch? Here, you can soak up the energy of Busan's tourist spots while getting some work done.

item.TITLE: DOMOHEON, a Space to “Promote” (domo in Korean) the Future of Busan Together
item.SUBTITLE: DOMOHEON
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 2, Namcheon Station, Busan Metro Line 2 -> A 9-minute walk (parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
DOMOHEON is a space that connects Busan’s past and future in a special way. The former Busan Mayor’s Residence has been remodeled into an open space for the public for walking, relaxation, and intellectual exchange.
The building has a lounge, a lecture hall, a meeting room, a multi-purpose space, a conference room, a shared office, and a children’s space named Deullak Nallak. The idea is to facilitate access to cultural programs and collaborations between local artists and entrepreneurs. 
In addition to the wonderful facilities, there are also high-quality programs. Check out the website for more information on the programs!
Outside the DONOHEON building, you’ll find Sosopung Garden stretched wide and trails. The Sosopung Garden is a public garden created by a public institution, so it’s open for citizens to visit and enjoy a picnic.
The first floor of DOMOHEON is home to the Domoheon Branch of Momos Coffee, Busan’s top coffee brand. After you’ve had a picnic or attended a program at DOMOHEON, you can relax and enjoy coffee and sweets here.
Visit DOMOHEON, a place where you can relax, connect, and brainstorm new ideas to shape Busan’s future together!

item.TITLE: Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum,'  Meeting Yeongdo in the Neolithic Age
item.SUBTITLE: Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 8, Nampo Station,  Busan Metro Line 1  → Bus No. 8, 30 or 190 from Yeongdodaegyo Bridge Station → Get off at Korea Maritime & Ocean University. Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum Station and 3- minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum is a great place to learn more about the Neolithic Dongsam-dong, Busan.
Walking along the coastal trail from Hari Port will take you there in no time. A shell midden is a heap of shellfish eaten and gathered by Aboriginal people dating back to the Neolithic Age, which is about 8,000 years ago. Dongsam-dong Shell Midden is one of the representative shell middens in Korea, and the exhibition hall displays some of the animal bones and living tools that were discovered from the midden. With a deeper knowledge of the Yeongdo area and its history in the Neolithic Age, Yeongdo Island and Dongsam-dong can be viewed from a new perspective.

item.TITLE: Busan Citizens Park History Museum: Learn All About the US Army Camp Hialeah
item.SUBTITLE: Busan Citizens Park History Museum
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 2, Bujeon Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line -> 14- minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The Busan Citizen Park History Museum showcases the 100-year history of Busan Citizens Park through exhibits and videos. With a variety of exhibitions and programs, visitors can explore Busan's poignant modern history and experience a journey back in time. The museum is divided into the Space of Memory and four exhibition halls. Explore the history of Busan in each hall and immerse yourself in the city’s past.

Space of Memory

The Space of Memory, a reinforced concrete building constructed in 1949, once served as a dining and banquet hall for the U.S. military officers. The markings and stars of the U.S. 8th Army on the ceiling vividly capture the atmosphere of that era. Today, it houses exhibition videos that explore the historical background of Busan Citizens Park.

Exhibition 1

Exhibition 1 highlights the transformation of farmland in Beomjeon-ri and Yeonji-ri, Busan, which was occupied by the Japanese during the Japanese colonial period. The Beomjeon-dong area was initially operated as a Seomyeon Racetrack for entertainment and military horse training, later becoming a Japanese military base and temporary training center. This exhibition offers insights into the area’s transformation and its historical significance.

Exhibition 2

Exhibition 2 focuses on the entry of U.S. forces into the Korean Peninsula after World War II and and the history of Camp Hialeah, which served as the Busan Base Command. Visitors can explore Camp Hialeah’s role as a military supply base through artifacts and models.

Exhibition 3

Exhibition 3 illustrates how a village south of Camp Hialeah was transformed by the presence of the U.S. military. It showcases the development of the town’s commercial district through its coexistence with the US military and provides a glimpse into the lives of residents during the boom years through detailed models.

Exhibition 4

Exhibition 4 explores the efforts of civic groups to reclaim the Camp Hialeah site and transform it into Busan Citizens Park. Through panels, videos, and interactive activities, visitors can learn about the actions taken to make this vision a reality.

item.TITLE: Dadaepo Badanuri-gil trail for a peaceful walk on a quiet beach
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Yim Seong-Hwan
item.TRFC_INFO: 1-minute walk from Exit 2, Hadan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. 61 from Hadan Station Transfer Center Stop -> Get off at Myeongwon Elementary School Stop -> 16-minute walk (parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Check out the Dadaepo Badanuri-gil Trail (East Coast), a peaceful trail where you can experience the beauty of the Dadaepo coast up close.
This trail, set against the stunning backdrop of Busan's sea, is perfect for a relaxing stroll. Walk along the wide beach, feel the cool sea breeze, and take in the ever-changing ocean views. Connected to Dadaepo Beach, it’s an ideal spot to fully enjoy the beauty of the sea.
The east coast trail is a fantastic place for a peaceful walk, running right along the coastline. Its quiet and serene atmosphere makes it perfect for a relaxing stroll. The promenade is lined with benches and shaded resting spots, offering plenty of opportunities to take a break. With the expansive sea as your backdrop, every corner of the trail is a picture-perfect spot for photography.
The east coast trail is a wonderful spot for a peaceful walk along the coastline. Its quiet and serene ambiance makes it ideal for a relaxing stroll. The promenade offers plenty of benches and shaded resting areas, perfect for taking a break. With the expansive sea as your backdrop, every corner of the trail is a fantastic photo opportunity. 
The trail is well-maintained, making it comfortable for everyone to enjoy. It’s a perfect spot for families, friends, and couples to take a leisurely stroll.
If you’re looking to escape the daily grind and reconnect with nature, walk along the Dadaepo Badanuri-gil Trail and take in the stunning beauty of Busan’s Sea.

item.TITLE: Gwangalli Golbang: A Perfect Place for Solo Drinks and Music
item.SUBTITLE: Gwangalli Golbang
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5, Gwangan Station, Busan Metro Line 2 → Bus No. 83 from Suyeong Middle School Station → 1-minute walk from Millak-dong Garage Station (Use public parking nearby)
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME:
Monday, Thursday, Friday 12:00~01:00 (Break Time 16:00~17:00)
Wednesday 12:00~23:00 (Break Time 16:00~17:00)
Saturday 11:00~01:00 (Break Time 14:30~15:00)
Sunday 15:00~01:00
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Looking for a quiet spot to drink? Check out 'Gwangalli Golbang' – the perfect place to enjoy your drink and focus on the music!

Gwangalli Golbang is a unique music bar designed for those who enjoy drinking alone. The atmosphere is intentionally quiet, with orders placed discreetly through Instagram DMs or KakaoTalk chat to minimize conversation noise. While it may not be ideal for those looking to chat over drinks, it's the perfect spot for solo drinkers who want to immerse themselves in the music, savor their drinks, and soak in the serene ambiance.

The bar operates on a 100% reservation basis to ensure minimal disruptions during your visit. For guests arriving early, there's also a designated waiting area designed as a photo zone, offering a fun and creative spot to take photos while you wait.

Seating options include recliner seats, VIP sofa seats, and bean bag seats. Recliner and sofa seats allow you to enjoy your pre-requested songs and videos, while the bean bag seats, though not available for song requests, provide a private, cozy space with an exclusive screen.
Each seat also comes with a guestbook, offering a glimpse into the thoughts and memories of previous visitors. Why not leave your own comment and contribute to the sentimental atmosphere of this unique solo drinking experience?
On days when you crave quiet moments with music and drinks, head to Gwangalli Golbang and immerse yourself in its serene atmosphere!

item.TITLE: Osiria Coastal Walk: Scenic Beauty and Folk Tales
item.SUBTITLE: Osiria Coastal Walk
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Osiria Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line -> Bus No. 1001 or 139 from Osiria Station → 13-minute walk from Doam Back Gate Station
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The Osiria Coastal Walk is a scenic trail that runs along the Gijang coastline, offering breathtaking views of the open sea. With charming shelters dotted along the path, it’s the perfect spot to pause and soak in the stunning natural surroundings. The tranquil promenade is a harmonious blend of coastal vistas, vibrant wildflowers, and lush pine forests, providing a serene escape into nature. Along the way, walkers can enjoy a panoramic view of Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, one of Gijang's most iconic and picturesque landmarks.

The Osiria Coastal Walk is a 2.1-km trail that winds its way through some of Gijang’s most captivating attractions, including Yongwangdan Altar, Orangdae, Turtle Rock, ANANTI COVE, Hilton Hotel Busan, and Dongam Village. Yongwangdan Altar is especially noteworthy for its distinctive appeal, as visitors can step inside this remarkable shrine. Dedicated to the Dragon King who guards the East Sea, Yongwangdan exudes a grand and mysterious atmosphere, making a must-see destination along the trail.

The name “Osiria” originates from the initials of two iconic landmarks: Orangdae, known for its breathtaking views within the tourist complex, and Sirangdae, which tells the enchanting love story of a dragon woman and a monk named Mirang. The name also carries the inviting message to “come” to Busan. Why not take a journey along the Osiria Coastal Walk, where stunning natural landscape and legendary historical sites converge? Immerse yourself in the beauty and history of this remarkable trail and enjoy a day of healing and relaxation to your heart's content.

item.TITLE: Hong-Ti Art Center: Cultivating the Growth of Local Art
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Yim Seong-hwan
item.TRFC_INFO: 1-minute walk from Exit 2, Dadaepo Harbor Station, Busan Metro Line 1→Bus No. 3 from Dadaepo Harbor Station Stop→Get off at Dadaepo Harbor Stop→Bus No. Saha-gu 5 or Saha-gu 3-1 from Dadae Culture & Sports Center Station Stop→Get off at Kumkang Kind Corporate. Hong-Ti Art Center Stop→1-minute walk (parking available)
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME: Monday – Saturday 10:00-18:00 (Open on Saturday only when there is an exhibition or event)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Explore Hong-Ti Art Center, a dynamic creative hub for local artists and the community.
The Hong-Ti Art Center is a creative space dedicated to visual installation art, serving as a vital cultural hub for local artists and supporting those based in Dadaepo.
It hosts a variety of exhibitions and programs, including relay solo exhibitions by artists in residence, contributing to a vibrant and dynamic art scene.

More than just an exhibition venue, the center fosters public engagement through open studios and cultural outreach programs that bring art closer to the community.
Exhibitions can also be enjoyed online, allowing you to experience art anytime, anywhere. Please note that the center is open for exhibitions and events only on Saturdays, so be sure to check ahead before visiting.

In front of the Hong-Ti Art Center lies Hongti Cultural Park, where you can enjoy a stroll through outdoor installations after viewing the exhibition. Nearby, the Hongti Art Village hosts additional exhibitions, offering a wide variety of artworks to explore.
Be sure to check their Instagram for the latest events and updates!

Discover a remarkable world of art where creativity and community come together.

item.TITLE: Ilgwang Mining Village: Where Beautiful Nature Meets Painful History
item.SUBTITLE: Photography by Yim Seong-Hwan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 7, Gijang Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line→Bus No. 182 from Gijang Market Station→Get off at Jwacheon Elementary School Station →4-minute walk→Bus No. 8-1 from Gijang-gun 8-1 from Jwacheon Elementary School Station→Mining Village Entrance Station→8-minute walk (Parking available – No designated parking space, parking along the road is possible)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Visit ‘Ilgwang Mining Village,’ a site with a history of forced labor.
Ilgwang Mining Village carries the painful legacy of forced labor during the Japanese colonial period. The scars of this history remain visible today. In the 1930s, Japan's Sumitomo Metal Mining Co, Ltd. developed the Nikko Mine (Ilgwang Mine) to exploit Korea’s copper resources. Mining operations began in 1937, and the mine became one of the country’s top five copper producers.
Starting in 1944, many Koreans were forcibly mobilized to work in copper mining and subjected to military training. The working conditions were extremely harsh, leading to immense suffering. As a result, Ilgwang Mining Village gained notoriety as a ‘hellhole workplace.’
At the entrance to the mine, you can still see remnants of the Japanese occupation, including the ruins of Japanese-style offices and houses once used by executives. Structures like laundries, wells, and communal toilets reflect the harsh conditions endured by forced laborers and offer a glimpse into their daily lives. 
Although the village has declined over time following the mine’s closure, it retains much of its original character, providing insight into how our ancestors lived during the Japanese occupation.
Beyond its historical significance, the site is also a picturesque agricultural complex, adorned with pink muhly and silver grass that create a stunning view in every season. Experience the echoes of your ancestors’ footsteps in this mining town where history and nature intertwine.

item.TITLE: Busan Port Pier 1: Where the Past Meets the Future
item.SUBTITLE: Photography by Yim Seong-Hwan
item.TRFC_INFO: 9-minute walk from Exit 2, Jungang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 (Parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
From the painful history of displaced people to the economic development of Busan, 'Busan Port Pier 1' symbolizes the beginning of reconstruction.
Busan Port Pier 1 has been a vital trade center since the Joseon Dynasty. Opened in 1876 under the Ganghwa Treaty, it gained historical significance alongside the development of Busan Port. During the Japanese colonial period, the completion of Pier 1 and the opening of the Gyeongbu Line Railway transformed it into a base for Japan's continental invasion and a hub for transporting military supplies.
During the Korean War, Pier 1 served as a vital passageway for evacuees, UN troops, and relief supplies. It became a symbol of hope for evacuees and a starting point for Busan’s rebuilding efforts. Additionally, it holds historical significance as a site for the transfer of North Korean and UN prisoners of war.
Today, Pier 1 is much more than a logistics port – it serves as a major hub for Korea's economic growth and a key link to the Busan New Port. The site, where the pain and hope of the past coexist, is gaining recognition as a cultural heritage site and is being considered for UNESCO listing. The large warehouses at Pier 1 also host international cultural events, such as the Busan International Photo Festival, enhancing its value as a space where tourism and culture converge.
Busan Port Pier 1 stands as a symbol of hope and reconstruction, shaping the city’s identity and development. Visit this historic site to experience its enduring legacy and reflect on its profound historical significance.

item.TITLE: United Nations Peace Memorial: A Tribute to the UN's Commitment and Promise of Peace
item.SUBTITLE: Photography by Yim Seong-Hwan
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5, Daeyeon Station, Busan Metro Line 2→Bus No. 138 from Daeyeon Station (Busan Bank)→Get off at UN Memorial Cemetery. Busan Cultural Center Station→10-minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Visit the United Nations Peace Memorial to delve deeper into the history of the Korean War.
The United Nations Peace Memorial explores a wide range of topics, including the causes and progression of the Korean War, the stories of the UN troops who fought in the conflict, and the United Nations’ vision today. It holds significant historical value, offering visitors a chance to reflect on the contributions of 26 allied countries and the veterans who worked for peace on the Korean Peninsula. Located in Busan, the memorial also features a section dedicated to the city’s role and significance as the ‘war capital.’
The first floor features exhibits detailing the unfolding of the Korean War, along with rooms showcasing preserved military items from the era. It offers a meaningful opportunity to reflect on the events of that time.
The exhibits on the second floor focus on the UN's role in the war and the remembrance of UN veterans. Items used by UN troops during the war are on display, offering visitors a chance to connect with and honor the veterans' legacy.
The magic art on the walls and floors, along with the Sibal car and the Retona - a real military vehicle model in the hallway - are particularly noteworthy, making history more engaging and accessible, especially for children.
The second floor also features the UN Kids Zone, where children can play with toys and read books, ensuring they stay entertained during their visit. There's also a coffee shop right right next to the Kids Zone, providing a perfect spot for weary parents to take a break.
In addition, the museum features detailed exhibits on the meaning and significance of the UN, its current vision, and the role of UNICEF. Visitors can also explore the Peace Message Zone, where they can leave messages of gratitude to the veterans.
The United Nations Peace Memorial is located just a short distance from the UN Memorial Cemetery, making it easy to visit both. After exploring the exhibits at the United Nations Peace Memorial, take a moment to pay your respects to the fallen at the UN Memorial Cemetery.

item.TITLE: Discover the Beauty of Winter Migratory Birds at the Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory
item.SUBTITLE: Photography by Mun Cheol-Jin
item.TRFC_INFO: 1-minute walk from Exit 5, Hadan Station, Busan Metro Line 1→ Bus No. 171 from Hadan Station Transfer Center→Get off at Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory Station →2-minute walk  (Parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Visit the Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory, a hidden gem in the Nakdonggang estuary. 
This is a prime birding site where around 150 species of migratory birds come to winter every year, offering a chance to witness the changing seasons alongside a variety of bird species.
From the observatory, you can observe migratory birds feeding on the mudflats up close, with spectacular winter displays by mallards, whooper swans, Saunders’s gulls, and other winter migrants.
Telescopes are available free of charge at the viewing platform, allowing you to get a closer look at the migratory birds. Signs along the path feature photos and descriptions of the birds to enrich your birdwatching experience. This spot is also popular with children, offering a chance to learn about migratory birds and aquatic plants up close. Remember to keep a respectful distance, as the birds can be startled if you get too close!
The Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory is also renowned for its stunning sunset views and attracts crowds on weekends, offering spectacular views of golden mudflats and migratory birds. It connects to the Ocean City Galmatgil Trails, making it a great place for a relaxing stroll.
For a quieter experience immersed in nature, theobservatory is a great place to create lasting memories.

item.TITLE: ‘Podium Dive M’, A Rising Cultural Arena In Gwangalli
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Shin Gyeong-Min
item.TRFC_INFO: 3-minute walk from Exit 5, Gwangan Station, Busan Metro Line 2 -> Bus No. 42 from Gwangalli Entrance Station-> Get off at Gwangil Mansion Station -> 1-minute walk (parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Podium Dive M is an exhibition complex that offers a variety of cultural experiences, including art, books, and coffee, all in one place. Its sensual interior and laid-back vibe make it a popular date spot. The building's unique structure with a hole in the center is pretty striking, and the sophisticated details make every corner a photo zone.
The journey begins on the first basement floor, where you'll find local content curation introducing restaurants and attractions near Gwangalli Beach. The second basement floor is home to an art gallery where you can enjoy a different exhibit each season. The third basement floor is where you'll find a bookstore and merchandise shop offering a great selection of books and accessories.
Experience the rich and varied culture at Podium Dive M. It's the perfect place to unwind while enjoying some artistic flair!

item.TITLE: Gallery Sujeong: Unveiling the Hidden Arts of Busan
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Mun Cheol-jin
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3, Choryang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. 52 from Choryang Station Exit 3 Stop -> Sujeong 4-dong Stop (Final stop) -> 1-minute walk (Parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Gallery Sujeong, located in Sujeong-dong, Dong-gu, Busan, is a special space renovated from a 50-year-old Sujeong apartment building. It provides a great platform for up-and-coming artists to showcase their work and exudes a unique old Busan vibe.

It is a ‘non-commercial alternative space’ that puts artists and local people before commercial interests, supporting artists in presenting their work and interacting with each other, thereby enhancing the significance of a gallery.

Take a moment to experience the unique blend of Busan's past and present, and feel its profound impact on you.

item.TITLE: Ibagu Camp: A Healing Space That Grows With The Village
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Mun Cheol-jin
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3, Choryang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. 52 from Choryang Station Exit 3 Stop -> Get off at Geumsusa Temple Stop -> 5-minute walk (Use a public parking lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Located on the Choryang Sanbok Road, Ibagu Camp is a guesthouse that blends urban regeneration with urban bed-and-breakfast experience. It's more than just a place to stay - it's a unique healing space developed with the locals, contributing to job creation in the village.

All rooms offer views of Busanhangdaegyo Bridge and the original city center, while the second-floor terrace provides barbecues and rooftop camping for a unique downtown camping experience. It is also close to the cypress forest, Democracy Park, and Gubongsan Healing Forest Trail, making it an ideal spot to enjoy nature.

It's perfect for those looking to escape the hustle and bustle of the city center and enjoy some time to themselves!

item.TITLE: DOT Museum: A Pause for Art in Everyday Life
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Jeong Ho-yun
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 5, Oncheonjang Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 203 from Oncheonjang Station Stop → Get off at Gwangmyeongsa Temple → 1-minute walk (Parking available)
item.HLDY_INFO: Every Sunday, Monday, January 1, and national holidays
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
As the fourth private art museum in Busan, the DOT Museum goes beyond exhibitions by supporting the work of local artists and offering residents opportunities to experience culture and art up close. With the slogan “Connecting Life and Art,” the museum embodies artistic values by fostering meaningful relationships between artists and visitors.
The museum holds at least two exhibitions annually to discover and showcase local artists, and it offers a variety of arts and cultural education programs, including one-day courses and humanities lectures, to expand residents’ access to the arts.

Discover a unique moment where art and everyday life merge at the DOT Museum.

item.TITLE: Following in the Footsteps of Conviction And Sacrifice, Oryundae Martyrs Shrine
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Jeong Ho-yun
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 4, Jangjeon Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. Geumjeong-gu 5 from Jangjeon Station Exit 4 Stop -> Get off at Oryundae Martyrs Shrine. Museum Stop -> 1-minute walk (Parking available and free parking at Oryun-dong Public Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The Oryundae Martyrs' Shrine is a significant place preserving the history of Korean Catholicism. It features the Martyrs' Cathedral, which houses the mausoleums of eight Busan martyrs and the remains of 26 Korean martyrs, along with the Korean Martyrs' Museum, showcasing various artefacts.
Behind the church lies the Way of the Cross, a symbolic walkway representing the sufferings of Jesus, leaving a profound impression with every step you take.

While the museum and Daeseongjeon Shrine are currently under construction, there are still plenty of other places to explore. Keep an open mind, embrace the unfamiliar, and discover how truly enlightening travel can be.

item.TITLE: Gallery Playlist, Busan's New Mecca for Contemporary Art
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Jeong Ho-yun
item.ADDR1: 1F, 3, Daecheong-ro 138beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan (Use Yongdusan Park Public Parking Lot)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Gallery Playlist, a private art museum located in Jung-gu, Busan, is a space that offers fresh inspiration for those who love contemporary art. It actively hosts exhibitions featuring various emerging contemporary artists, expanding the range of art on display in Busan.

To the left of the entrance is a guest book and artists' biographies, while the interior of the gallery is minimalist and distinctive in its design. The exhibits are further enhanced by the creative layout and design of the space.

If you're looking for a deep dive into contemporary art in Busan, Gallery Playlist is a must-visit.

item.TITLE: Yeongdo Sunrise Observatory
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 8, Nampo Station, Busan Metro Line 1  →  Bus No. 5 from Yeongdodaegyo Bridge. Nampo Station Stop  → 2-minute walk from Ssangyong Driving Academy Stop
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Sunrise Observatory located at the top of a quiet village is a perfect place for those who want to enjoy their solitude.
If you climb up slowly along the alleyway of the village, you will see a white observatory. It may be a little scary because the building is dim inside, but as soon as you enter, the sensor light detects movement and lights up brightly. On taking steps up to the rooftop equivalent to the third-floor height, you will find yourself in a completely new world.


The feeling of fear flies off when you see the open scenery of Busanhangdaegyo Bridge. The time spent grumbling while climbing up the rather long uphill disappears from your memory. From Cheonghak-dong right in front to Busanhangdaegyo Bridge shining in five colors and Busan International Passenger Terminal, the warm night view is enchanting. A beautiful serenity surrounds you. Now all you have to do is to spend some quite time for yourself.

item.TITLE: A peaceful New Year's Eve at Haegwangsa Temple, a tranquil seaside temple
item.SUBTITLE: Photography by Shin Gyeong-min
item.TRFC_INFO: 1-minute walk from Exit 1, Osiria Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line -> Bus No. 61 from Osiria Station Stop -> 3-minute walk from Haegwangsa Temple Stop (parking available)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Haegwangsa Temple was named with a combination of "hae," meaning wisdom as wide and deep as the sea, and "gwang," meaning light that illuminates the path of sentient beings. Although small in size, the temple is full of Buddhist-style architecture and cultural artifacts of religious significance, making it a great place to experience Buddhist culture up close.
In particular, the temple is located near Orangdae Park, a famous sunrise viewing spot, making it a great place to watch the sunrise while making a New Year's wish. The overall atmosphere is quiet and peaceful, so it is recommended for those who want to start the year in peace. It would be even more meaningful to make a New Year's wish at the Yongwangdan Altar at Haegwangsa Temple in Orangdae Park.

If you want to find peace of mind in the New Year, prepare for a new beginning at Haegwangsa Temple, a temple that harmonizes with the sea!

item.TITLE: Ryun Village: Where Forest Relaxation Meets Culture
item.SUBTITLE: An Eco-Friendly Cultural Community, Ryun Village
item.TRFC_INFO: 1-minute walk from Exit 4, Jangjeon Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. Geumjeong-gu 5 from Jangjeon Station Exit 4 Stop -> Get off at Oryun Bon-dong Village Stop -> 1-minute walk (Parking available)
item.HLDY_INFO: Please check our Instagram for updates on reduced opening hours, irregular closures and more.
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Ryun Village, once a mushroom farm, has been transformed into a warehouse-style café and eco-cultural space. The first and second floors serve as cafes and co-working spaces, while the third floor functions as a workation center.

It collaborates with vegan restaurant Nayuta's Kitchen and farmers' markets to promote an eco-friendly lifestyle. On the second Monday of every month, it also hosts a Forest Wellness program, popular among wellness seekers looking to reconnect with nature, featuring activities such as Wellness Retreat and aroma pilates.

The Ttangmoesan Red Clay Trail, Galmaet-gil and Hoedong Reservoir are also nearby, offering a great variety of walking options. So why not combine nature and culture?

item.TITLE: Naewonjeongsa Temple
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3, Seodaesin Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Transfer to Bus No. Seo-gu 1 at Seodaesin Station Bus Stop → Get off at Gudeok Kkonmaeul Bus Stop, an 11-min walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Temple stay is one of the representative healing experiences that cannot be missed in wellness tourism. Did you know that it is also possible in Busan?

Naewonjeongsa Temple, located at the foot of Gudeoksan Mountain, has a temple stay living center and an international meditation healing center, allowing for a variety of wellness experiences.

At Naewonjeongsa Temple, where you can breathe clean air in nature while being highly accessible, not far from the city, you can feel the unique charm of a temple stay, where you can escape from daily life and concentrate on yourself.

item.TITLE: Hongbeopsa Temple
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 3, Nopo Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Transfer to Bus No. Geumjeon-gu 2-2 at Busan Central Bus Terminal and Nopo Station Bus Stop -> Get off at Jo-ri Senior Center Bus Stop, a 3-min walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Hongbeopsa Temple is the temple where the largest seated Buddha statue in Korea is located. 

In this place, you can have singing bowl healing meditation, and temple stay. The singing bowl, a traditional Tibetan instrument, is one of the representative wellness experiences as the sound resonates when tapping or rubbing the surface to bring comfort.

In particular, Hongbeopsa Temple is equipped with an infrastructure for English interpreters and overseas travel guides, so foreigners can visit and have a wellness experience whenever they want.

item.TITLE: Busan Children's Grand Park Healing Forest
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 7, Bujeon Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Transfer to Bus No. 33 at Songsanghyeon Square Bus Stop >  Get off at Choeup Samgeori Bus Stop, a 6-min walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Is there anyone who only thinks of nature that is distant from the city when it comes to wellness? You can find a forest even in the middle of the city.

There is a healing forest inside Busan Children’s Grand Park located in Busanjin-gu, where you can see a large size of cypress forest. 

Why don’t you enjoy the beauty of nature wherever you go, and visit Seongjigok Valley Reservoir, a national cultural asset located inside Children’s Grand Park?

item.TITLE: Dongbaekseom Island: Where Natural Beauty and History Come Together
item.SUBTITLE: Dongbaekseom Island
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Dongbaek Station, Busan Metro Line 2 → 17-minute walk
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Dongbaekseom Island has long been admired for its beauty. Although it has been connected to the mainland by sedimentation over the years, it still retains the name 'island' and traces of its ancient topography. The name “Haeundae” comes from the fact that the Silla-era scholar Choi Chi-won, who admired the beauty of the island, carved his own name on a rock, and the landscape has long been renowned for its outstanding beauty.
There are many historical symbols, so it is fun to look around. There are various attractions, including the legendary Princess Hwangok Mermaid Statue and the Nurimaru APEC House, where the 2005 APEC Summit was held. You can also enjoy the magnificent scenery of camellias in full bloom from winter to spring.

Make many fond memories on Dongbaekseom Island, where you can enjoy its awe-inspiring natural scenery and interesting history together!

item.TITLE: A Special Trip to Jungsado, an Island with a Beautiful View of the Nakdonggang River.
item.SUBTITLE: Jungsado Village
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Buram Station, Busan-Gimhae Light Rail Transit Line of Busan Metro → Bus From Buram-dong Community Center Stop → 15-minute walk from Simangyo Bridge
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Jungsado Island in Gangseo-gu, Busan offers a panoramic view of the Nakdonggang River. 
It has recently become a popular camping spot. It is a favorite among campers because there are many large areas that make it easy to set up tents. It is also attractive because the unadorned natural scenery has been preserved.

There are many activities to enjoy including camping, riverside walks, and cycling. It is also a popular fishing spot for anglers. It is the perfect place for those who love nature tourism. However, there are no amenities such as supermarkets or convenience stores nearby, so it is recommended to prepare the necessary items in advance.

If you explore the surroundings of the island, you will see several cafes. After camping or hiking, you can stop at a cafe for a unique and relaxing experience. Enjoy a special nature trip to Jungsado, an island with a beautiful river view!

item.TITLE: BNK Busan Bank Art Cinema Corner Theater: An independent Cinema in Busan’s Original City Center
item.SUBTITLE: BNK Busan Bank Art Cinema Corner Theater
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Nampo Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → 7-minute
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
BNK Busan Bank Art Cinema Corner Theater is a small cinema that mainly shows rare films, including independent films and classic masterpieces. You can enjoy high-quality films at affordable prices: KRW 5,000 for seniors, KRW 7,000 for teenagers, and KRW 8,000 for adults.

The Corner Theater is not just a theater, but a 'Cinema-People-Tech' theater that screens, records, and restores the voices of the audience. As such, it is recommended for those seeking a unique film experience, as it allows them to share their in-depth views on films.

In addition to the Corner Theater, BNK Busan Bank Art Cinema has various cultural and art spaces. You can also explore a variety of cultural content at a youth cultural space called ‘Cheongnyeon Jakdangso’ and a souvenir shop called ‘Geumjiogyeop.’

BNK Busan Bank Art Cinema Corner Theater is a place where you can enjoy various cultural arts while watching great movies at a reasonable price! If you’re looking for more than just watching a film, this is the place to be!

item.TITLE: Youngju Mansion: Where the Traces of Life Becomes Art
item.SUBTITLE: Youngju Mansion
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 1, Busan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 43 from Busan Station Stop → 1-minute walk from Dong-A Apt. Stop
item.USAGE_DAY_WEEK_AND_TIME: Open during the exhibition period: Everyday 10:00~18:00
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
In the middle of Busan's original downtown, there is a place where time seems to have stood still. It is Youngju Mansion, an art exhibition space located in Youngju Apartment, which has a long history. Once a private 'home,' it has been transformed into an 'exhibition space,' offering fascinating to experience of art where the past and present intersect, rather than just a traditional exhibition.

Youngju Mansion hosts various exhibitions that interpret small-scale events into art by artists working in Busan. The building is free to visit and there is no caretaker on site, so anyone can freely explore the space and experience the atmosphere of Youngju Mansion. The old building's features have been kept and the space itself feels like an exhibition. The surrounding landscape also retains the charm of Busan's old downtown.

Come and see Youngju Mansion, an exhibition space where the aged and worn surroundings themselves become art.

* Refer to the Instagram (@youngjumansion), which is available only during the exhibition period.

item.TITLE: Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park: Get Some Exercise in the City Center
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Mun Cheol-jin
item.TRFC_INFO: Exit 2, Bujeon Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. Busanjin-gu 2 from Bujeon Station Stop -> 17-minute walk from Daesan Apt. Stop
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park is a great place to enjoy sports in the fresh air. It's a popular place for an everyday workout because of its convenient location close to the city center. It's got all sorts of sports facilities, like a soccer field, wrestling ring, tennis court, badminton court, and a gateball field, so there's something for everyone.

The main place here is the big sports ground, which is 200 meters up in the air. It's the highest soccer field in Busan, and you can enjoy soccer in a unique way while looking down on the Seomyeon area. It also has artificial turf, which makes it safer to play on.

There's also Hwangnyeongsan Eco Play Park, making it a great place to visit as a family. It's got all sorts of fun play equipment like slides, stepping stones, and more, making it the perfect place for children to play outdoors.

Some of the sports facilities require advance reservations, but you can easily reserve your favorite spot via the Busanjin-gu Office website.

If you're looking for an invigorating workout in the middle of nature, Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park is the place to be!

item.TITLE: Get to Know More About Buddhist Culture at the Beomeosa Seongbo Museum
item.SUBTITLE: Photographed by Shin Gyeong-min
item.TRFC_INFO:
Exit 7, Beomeosa Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 90 from Beomeosa Temple Entrance 
Stop → 1-minute walk from Sangma Village. Beomeosa Temple Museum Stop
item.HLDY_INFO: Every Monday, Lunar New Year and Chuseok holidays
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Check out Beomeosa Seongbo Museum, a hidden gem in Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Seongbo Museum is a place that displays treasures and artefacts related to Buddha and Buddhism. The Beomeosa Seongbo Museum is a great place to learn more about Buddhism, with a range of valuable Buddhist artifacts, like Buddha statues and paintings, all in one place.


When you go into the permanent exhibition hall on the first floor, you can see the history of Beomeosa Temple and the traces of its past chief monks on both walls. The entrance is also home to the Sacred Bell of Great King Seongdeok, which serves as a meaningful starting point for visitors to the museum, giving them a glimpse into the long history of the temple.

The paintings in the exhibition are all in great condition, making them easy for visitors unfamiliar with Buddhism to appreciate. The basic teachings and historical records of Buddhism are well organized, too. If you want a deeper understanding of the exhibition, it's a good idea to pick up a pamphlet at the information desk at the entrance, and read it carefully before exploring.

The museum is free to visit, which makes it even more accessible. It's open until 5 p.m., but it's best to get there before 4 p.m., so you can take your time and enjoy everything. Just remember that you can't take photos in the museum without permission.

When you need a break, why not visit the Beomeosa Seongbo Museum to learn about the history and culture of the area?

item.TITLE: Daeryong Village in Gijang - Where Art Blooms Around Every Corner
item.ADDR1: 17, Daeryong 1-gil, Jangan-eup, Gijang-gun, Busan, Republic of Korea
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Located in Ori, Jangan-eup, Gijang-gun, Busan, Daeryong Village is a peaceful rural community where nature, tradition, and art come together in harmony. Its name, “Daeryong” (meaning “great dragon”), comes from a local legend about a giant dragon that once lived in a pond near the village entrance. Quiet and cozy, this rural village offers a tranquil escape just beyond the bustle of central Busan.
In 2007, as part of the “Better Living Environment” project, artists began moving into the village—marking the beginning of its transformation. Empty lots and old houses were gradually turned into studios and exhibition spaces, and over time, the entire village naturally evolved into what is now known as an “art village.”
Even today, the village feels more like an open-air gallery than a quiet countryside town.
Murals on building walls, sculptures tucked into alleyways, and various artworks you encounter along the way all come together to create a uniquely artistic atmosphere that stirs the senses.


One of the village’s most beloved spots was the self-service café Art in Ori, known for its charming interior, handwritten notes left by visitors, and the many artworks that filled the space. Together, they created a warm, sentimental atmosphere that made it a must-visit destination in Daeryong Village.

Although the café is no longer in operation, the village still continues to attract visitors with experiences like wood-fired pizza-making, occasional flea markets, and cultural events.

Daeryong Village continues to offer visitors a unique experience—encountering art in the heart of nature. If you're visiting Gijang in Busan, why not spend a quiet, relaxing day in this charming art village, away from the fast pace of the city?

item.TITLE: Nampo & Gwangbok Underground Shopping Centers
item.ADDR1:
Nampo Underground Shopping Center : B1, 44, Gudeok-ro, Jung-gu, Busan (Nampo-dong 5-ga)
Gwangbok Underground Shopping Center : 8, Jungang-daero 29beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan (Jungang-dong 1-ga)
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Nampo & Gwangbok Underground Shopping Centers were established in the early 1980s and have since become key commercial hubs in the area. Located near Nampo Station and Jagalchi Station, two of Busan's major transit points, they have grown thanks to high foot traffic and vibrant local business districts.
 At one time, it was no exaggeration to say that every young person in Busan passed through these underground shopping centers. Once the heart of the city’s fashion scene, they were packed with trendy clothing stores and bustling with crowds of shoppers. Often called the “underground Myeong-dong,” they were the go-to spots for the latest styles and stood as cultural icons for Busan’s youth.

 Although the cultural spotlight has shifted to newer areas like Haeundae and Gwangalli, and their former glory has somewhat faded, these underground shopping centers remain nostalgic for the older generation, serving like time machines filled with familiarity and warmth. Rich with stories from the past, they continue to be a part of everyday life for the people of Busan.

item.TITLE: Panoramic Busan: Hwangnyeongsan Viewing Lounge Drive
item.ADDR1: San 50-18, Jeonpo-dong, Busanjin-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
How about taking in the cityscape from one of Busan’s hidden gems, the Hwangnyeongsan Viewing Lounge? From here, you can enjoy views of Gwangandaegyo Bridge, Haeundae, and Busan Port, making it the perfect spot to take in Busan’s stunning night skyline.
You can reach the Hwangnyeongsan Viewing Lounge either by hiking the trail or by taking a leisurely drive along the paved road that leads near the peak. From the parking area, it’s just a 10-minute walk before the sweeping views unfold. At the top, a spacious viewing deck offers a relaxing spot to take in the scenery and snap unforgettable photos.
At the summit, you'll find the Hwangnyeongsan Beacon Mound. During the Joseon Dynasty, smoke and fire signals here warned nearby regions of invasions or emergencies. Just a short walk from the viewing lounge, it adds a layer of history to your visit and is well worth seeing.
Famed for its stunning sunsets and night views, this spot is the perfect place to experience Busan’s history, nature, and cityscape all at once.

item.TITLE: 1934 Train Dongnae Station
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The 1934 Dongnae Station Exhibition Hall, located in Dongnae-gu, Busan, is a historical and cultural space that reopened in 2025 after remodeling the former Dongnae Station of the Donghae Nambu Line. Its name comes from the year the station was built, 1934, and the site also carries the painful history of being used during the Japanese colonial period for colonial rule and resource exploitation.
In the exhibition space, which makes use of the old waiting room, visitors can explore the history of railway development, records of events related to Dongnae Station, and stories of local independence movements such as student protests. The former office area is filled with photographs and documents depicting life in the 1950s and 1960s. There are also interactive programs, including a zone where visitors can try on a station master’s uniform, guided tours by cultural interpreters, and photo zones for commemorative pictures.
Outside, a steam locomotive and sculptures are on display, creating a unique atmosphere where the past and present come together. More than a simple exhibition, the venue serves as a valuable cultural space where visitors can vividly experience the roots of Busan’s railway and the lives of its local people.

item.TITLE: Daehang Port East Breakwater Lighthouse—Where the Sea of Gadeokdo Island Ends
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
A hidden gem of Gadeokdo Island, the Daehang Port East Breakwater Lighthouse stands at the tranquil edge of the sea, greeting travelers as they arrive. The white lighthouse to the south and the red one to the north face each other across the water, quietly keeping watch over the coast together.
As the sun sets, the lighthouse glows against the crimson sky, painting a picture-perfect scene over the wide-open sea. It’s also a favorite spot for fishing. When you need a break from the city and want a serene place to watch the waves, the small lighthouse at the end of Daehang Port East Breakwater will be there to calm your heart.

item.TITLE: Chungmu-dong Coastal Market—Where the Sea Breeze Mingles with the Buzz of Everyday Life
item.TRFC_INFO: 122 meters from Exit 2 of Jagalchi Station
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Tucked away in Chungmu-dong, Seo-gu, Busan, the Coastal Market is where the city’s portside charm truly comes alive. Its location near Namhang Port made it easy to source fresh seafood, and over time, small shops began to gather, serving local fishermen and sailors. In the early 1960s, the market opened only at dawn, but by 1965, it had grown into the official Chungmu-dong Coastal Market we know today.
Set between Jagalchi Market and Namhang Port, this market is alive with the scent of the sea and the energy of daily life. Fresh seafood lines the stalls, while alleys filled with grilled eel, handmade noodles, butcher shops, and clothing stores create a colorful local scene. Every corner hums with voices and sea breezes that make you want to slow down and stay awhile.
There is a small lookout on one side of the market where you can take in views of Namhang Port—a nice spot to pause after wandering through the stalls. Although not a glamorous place, it’s where you’ll find the real Busan, alive with everyday moments. If you want to feel the city’s true charm, where the sea breeze and the warmth of its people come together, make your way to Chungmu-dong Coastal Market.

item.TITLE: Choryang Ibagu-gil: A Storytelling Walk through History
item.TRFC_INFO: 758 m from Exit 5 of Busan Station
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
The word “Ibagu” in Choryang Ibagu-gil means 'story' in the Busan dialect—and this hillside trail truly lives up to its name. Overlooking Busan Port, the path took shape when refugees from across the country settled here during the Korean War. Even today, traces of their lives remain in the old houses and winding alleyways that hold the spirit of the past.
One of the best-known spots along the trail, the 168 Stairs, was once part of the refugees’ daily climb. Now equipped with a monorail, it offers a fun and memorable way to experience the hillside. At the Ibagu Crafts Workshop, old photos and everyday objects from local residents bring Choryang’s past to life. The Wall Gallery and Mural Street add a creative touch, where the charm of old alleyways meets a modern artistic vibe.
From the observatory halfway up the hill, you’ll find breathtaking views of Busan Port and the city spread out below. The trail is especially beautiful at sunset, when the harbor glows in shades of gold and orange. Choryang Ibagu-gil is where the past and present meet—a living walkway that lets you experience Busan’s history and stories along the way.

item.TITLE: Hoedong Reservoir Trail: A Lakeside Walk in the Heart of the City
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
Hoedong Reservoir offers a quiet lakeside getaway just a short drive from the city. A neatly maintained trail wraps around the water, making it an easy, relaxing walk for all visitors. As you follow the path, you’ll notice how the scenery changes with the seasons and enjoy sweeping views of Geumjeongsan Mountain in the distance.
You’ll also find a stretch of soft red-clay path perfect for a refreshing barefoot walk, and a cypress woodland trail where you can breathe in the fresh forest air. Once you reach the Oryundae Observatory, the entire reservoir spreads out below, with a view that even resembles the shape of the Korean Peninsula.
If you’re looking to step away from your routine, Hoedong Reservoir offers just the right dose of nature and tranquility to truly unwind.

item.TITLE: The Little Prince House in Gamcheon Culture Village
item.SUBTITLE: Asia’s only permanent cultural exhibition space dedicated to The Little Prince
item.ITEMCNTNTS:
First published in New York in 1943, The Little Prince continues to be cherished by readers around the world today. Told through the innocent eyes of the Little Prince, the tale offers a pure perspective on the world and has touched the hearts of generations. In Busan’s Gamcheon Culture Village, a statue of the young protagonist reflects that same spirit and has become one of the most popular photo spots for visitors.
A new space inspired by this beloved tale—The Little Prince House—will open in Gamcheon Culture Village on March 18, 2026. As Asia’s only official permanent exhibition and cultural space dedicated to the classic work, it carries special significance with official recognition from 
the Antoine de Saint-Exupéry Youth Foundation in France, the homeland of the Little Prince.
At Little Prince House, a media art zone themed around the desert and the rose invites visitors into the world of the story. A stained-glass gallery and hands-on exhibition space offer a unique way to experience its themes, while a photo spot featuring the Little Prince allows visitors to capture the colorful scenery of Gamcheon Culture Village.
To celebrate the opening, a special ceremony will take place at 3:00 PM on March 18. Visitors are invited to spend a memorable time in Gamcheon Culture Village while reflecting on the message conveyed through The Little Prince and its author, Antoine de Saint-Exupéry.
